17680.title: Who is Behind the Avatar?  Verifying Teleoperator Identity in Reenacted Avatar Videos
17680.description: Welcome to the first International Competition on Verifying Teleoperator Identity in Reenacted Avatar Videos. The competition will be in conjunction with [ACCV2026](https://https://accv2026.org/])
17680.description_zh: 欢迎来到首届"重演化身视频中远程操作者身份验证"国际竞赛。本竞赛将与[ACCV2026](https://https://accv2026.org/)联合举办。

pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
Welcome to the first International Competition on **Teleoperator Identity Verification in Reenacted Avatar Videos (Who Is Behind the Avatar?)— WBA2026 @ ACCV, Osaka, Japan**. ## Motivation Photorealistic avatars are increasingly used in telepresence, mixed reality, gaming, virtual environments, and AI-mediated video communication. In these settings, the visible face may be synthetic or may differ entirely from the person controlling it. Consequently, conventional face-recognition methods may not be sufficient to verify the identity of the underlying user. The **WBA** competition investigates whether behavioral information preserved in avatar videos can be used to authenticate the human teleoperator independently of the avatar’s visual appearance. Unlike conventional DeepFake-detection challenges, **WBA** does not ask participants to determine whether a video is real or synthetic. Avatar-generated videos are treated as legitimate communication media. The objective is instead to verify **operator authenticity**: whether an avatar is controlled by the authorized person. ## Challenge Task
**WBA** is a **cross-avatar teleoperator verification challenge**. For each verification trial, participants are provided with: * A gallery avatar video driven by a known teleoperator * A probe avatar video driven by an unknown teleoperator. Participants must determine whether the two avatar videos are driven by: * **Same teleoperator**, representing a genuine trial * **Different teleoperators**, representing an Imposter trial The gallery and probe videos may represent the same person through different avatar identities. Therefore, systems should focus on teleoperator-specific behavioral information rather than the visible appearance of the avatar. Potential behavioral cues include: * facial-motion dynamics * head movement and pose * expression timing * gaze behavior * speech-related facial movement * temporal motion patterns * other person-specific behavioral characteristics Participants may develop systems using RGB video, facial landmarks, head-pose features, expression dynamics, temporal motion descriptors, video embeddings, or other suitable representations. ## Dataset The source driving videos were collected in Japan during controlled dyadic online first-meeting conversations. The selected sequences are taken from the self-introduction portion of the conversations and include both speaking and listening segments. The original recordings were captured under controlled frontal-camera and lighting conditions. However, the original human videos are retained by the organizers and are not released to challenge participants. Instead, the motion and expression information from the original recordings are transferred to photorealistic avatar templates through a face-reenactment pipeline. The avatar appearances are selected from the publicly available **NVFAIR** dataset. This design reduces the direct exposure of the original participants’ visual identities while preserving motion and behavioral information relevant to teleoperator verification.
pages.content_zh: 欢迎来到首届**重演头像视频中的远程操作者身份验证国际竞赛——WBA 2026**。 ## 动机 超逼真头像越来越多地被应用于远程呈现、混合现实、游戏、虚拟环境和人工智能中介的视频通信。在这些应用中，可见的面孔可能是合成的，或者可能与控制它的人完全不同。因此，传统的面部识别方法可能不足以验证底层用户的身份。 **谁在头像后面？(WBA)** 挑战赛调查了头像视频中保留的行为信息是否可以用于独立于头像视觉外观的人类远程操作者身份认证。 与传统的深伪检测挑战不同，WBA不要求参与者判断视频是否真实或合成。头像生成的视频被视为合法的通信媒介。目标是验证**操作者的真实性**：头像是否由授权人员控制。 ## 挑战任务 WBA 2026是一项**跨头像远程操作者验证挑战**。 对于每次验证试验，参与者获得： 1. 由已知远程操作者驱动的图库头像视频；以及 2. 由未知远程操作者驱动的探针头像视频。 参与者必须确定这两个头像视频是否由以下任一情况驱动： * **相同的远程操作者**，代表真实试验；或 * **不同的远程操作者**，代表冒充试验。 图库和探针视频可能通过不同的头像身份代表同一个人。因此，系统应专注于远程操作者特定的行为信息，而不是头像的可见外观。 潜在的行为线索包括： * 面部运动动态 * 头部运动和姿态 * 表情时序 * 注视行为 * 与语音相关的面部运动 * 时间运动模式 * 其他人员特定的行为特征 参与者可以使用RGB视频、面部特征点、头部姿态特征、表情动态、时间运动描述符、视频嵌入或其他合适的表示方法开发系统。 ## 数据集 源驱动视频是在日本进行的受控二人组在线首次会面对话期间收集的。所选序列取自对话的自我介绍部分，包括说话和聆听片段。 原始录制是在受控的正面摄像头和照明条件下捕获的。但是，原始人类视频由组织者保留，不会向挑战参与者发布。 相反，来自原始录制的运动和表情信息通过人脸重演管道转移到超逼真头像模板。头像外观选自公开可用的 **NVFAIR** 数据集，而重演视频使用 **GAGAvatar** 生成。 这种设计减少了原始参与者视觉身份的直接暴露，同时保留了与远程操作者验证相关的运动和行为信息。 所发布的数据集中不包含音频，评估期间也不使用音频。

pages.content: ### How to participate? Please register using your institutional email. Registrations with gmail.com or qq.com email addresses will not be approved. You can download the agreement from [here](http://www.am.sanken.osaka-u.ac.jp/BiometricDB/dataset/Competition/WBA2026/WBA_ACCV_2026%20Competition_License%20Agreement.pdf). After the organizers verify the signed agreement they will send a link to download the data. Important: the dataset will be provided exclusively to registered participating teams and is strictly limited to use for the challenge.. If you have any questions or need further assistance, please don’t hesitate to reach out to alsherfawi@yy.d3c.osaka-u.ac.jp and cc: allam@yy.d3c.osaka-u.ac.jp #### Released Resources The organizers plan to provide: Data: * labeled training data (re-enacted videos and landmarks) * test data (for submission) * a sample submission [Starter kit](https://github.com/jasam-sheja/wba-starter) * evaluation code on validation subset * a submission-validation tool The baseline system is intended to support reproducibility, reduce the entry barrier, and encourage participants to investigate stronger temporal and behavioral representations. Follow the instructions in the [starter kit](https://github.com/jasam-sheja/wba-starter) to prepare the data for training. #### Data-Use Policy The challenge data may only be used in accordance with the official WBA 2026 participation rules and the provided license agreement associated with the source datasets and avatar-generation resources. Participants must not attempt to recover, identify, manually label, or disclose the identities of individuals represented in the hidden evaluation data. Access to hidden labels, avatar-template identities, or unauthorized annotations is prohibited. ### Workshop Paper Submission Paper submission to the associated ACCV workshop is open to competition participants as well as non-participants. For competition participants, submission of a workshop paper is required in order to be considered for a competition award.. Papers from the winning teams will undergo a competition-oriented review, with particular consideration given to the technical description of the submitted system and its competition performance. Papers from non-winning teams and non-participants will be reviewed primarily on their scientific novelty, technical contribution, experimental evaluation, and overall research quality. Paper acceptance is not determined solely by competition ranking.

pages.title: Submission
pages.content: ## Training and Test Protocol The training and test sets are disjoint with respect to both: * teleoperator identity; and * avatar appearance. No teleoperator appearing in the test set is included in the training set. Similarly, the avatar templates used for testing are not included in the training data. This protocol evaluates whether submitted systems can generalize to: * unseen teleoperators; * unseen avatar identities; * different speaking conditions; * variations in avatar geometry and motion response. The challenge is designed to discourage reliance on avatar appearance and encourage the development of representations that capture persistent teleoperator-specific behavioral characteristics. ## Submission Important: For a submission to be considered valid, all models used must be trained exclusively on the provided training data. Submissions must not rely on external datasets, external models, pretrained models trained on other datasets, or any similar external resources. . Participants are required to generate and submit an embedding for every test video. For each verification pair, the submitted gallery and probe embeddings are compared using one of the following measures: * cosine similarity or cosine distance; or * Euclidean distance. Participants specify the comparison method used by their system at submission time. ## Evaluation The official evaluation metrics is **Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve — AUC** EER is reported as an additional reference metric and is not used to determine the final leaderboard ranking. Performance is evaluated under three conditions: ### Speaking Condition Both the gallery and probe videos contain speaking sequences. ### Non-Speaking Condition Both the gallery and probe videos contain listening or non-speaking sequences. ### Cross-Condition One video contains a speaking sequence, while the other contains a non-speaking sequence. The final leaderboard score is calculated as the **average AUC across the three evaluation conditions**.
pages.content_zh:
## 训练和测试协议

训练集和测试集在以下两个方面是互不相交的：

* 遥操作员身份；以及
* 虚拟形象外观。

测试集中出现的任何遥操作员都不包含在训练集中。同样，用于测试的虚拟形象模板不包含在训练数据中。

该协议评估提交的系统是否能够泛化到：

* 未见过的遥操作员；
* 未见过的虚拟形象身份；
* 不同的说话条件；
* 虚拟形象几何形状和运动响应的变化。

该挑战旨在抑制对虚拟形象外观的依赖，并鼓励开发能够捕捉持久遥操作员特定行为特征的表示方法。

## 提交

参赛者需要为每个测试视频生成并提交一个嵌入向量。

对于每对验证样本，提交的库嵌入和探针嵌入使用以下度量之一进行比较：

* 余弦相似度或余弦距离；或
* 欧几里得距离。

参赛者在提交时指定其系统使用的比较方法。

Codabench评估程序从提交的嵌入向量计算验证得分和相应的性能指标。

## 评估

官方评估指标包括：

* **受试者工作特征曲线下面积 — AUC**
* **等错误率 — EER**

团队的排名仅根据 **AUC** 确定。

EER作为附加参考指标报告，不用于确定最终排行榜排名。

性能在三种条件下进行评估：

### 说话条件

库视频和探针视频都包含说话序列。

### 非说话条件

库视频和探针视频都包含聆听或非说话序列。

### 交叉条件

一个视频包含说话序列，另一个包含非说话序列。

最终排行榜得分计算为**三种评估条件下的平均AUC**。

About

Datathon@IndoML 2026 is a research-oriented data science competition held in conjunction with IndoML 2026. This year's datathon challenges participants to tackle noise event detection and removal in real-world Indic speech — a critical problem for inclusive, robust Automatic Speech Recognition across Indian languages.

Track 1 — Detection

Detect noise events in Indic speech recordings with precise onset/offset timestamps. Effectively utilise data annotated at different levels (Gold / Silver / Bronze) to build robust noise-event detection systems.

The withheld test set (11 h) contains 7 h of natural (real-world) clips and 4 h of synthetic clips (clean speech with noise added synthetically). Track 1 is scored on the full 11 h combined; a natural/synthetic breakdown is reported for transparency only. Training data (~150 h across Gold/Silver/Bronze tiers) is available on Hugging Face: ARTPARK-IISc/Vaani-Noise-Event-Dataset (download code included there; image files are not required for this track).

Speech recordings collected in real Indian environments are dominated by non-stationary background events — vehicle horns, dogs barking, children crying, doorbells, ringtones, kitchen appliances, and devotional music. These events degrade downstream ASR.

Motivation

Most academic speech enhancement benchmarks are built around stationary noise (white, pink, café hum) or studio-recorded mixtures. Field recordings from rural and semi-urban India contain bursty, semantically rich events — a passing motorbike, a hen, a pressure-cooker whistle, a doorbell, a TV in another room — that current denoisers either smear over or treat as speech.

Two consequences follow:

  • Downstream ASR fails disproportionately on speakers from these environments, amplifying the existing performance gap between high-resource and low-resource Indic languages.
  • Standard sound-event detection (SED) datasets (AudioSet, DESED, DCASE) under-represent both Indian acoustic contexts and Indian speech, making transfer learning from them brittle.

This challenge targets that gap directly. It asks participants to treat noise as a first-class, labelled, time-localised object.

Responsible AI Alignment

This challenge is positioned under the Responsible AI track on three explicit axes:

  • Robustness — Real-world Indic recordings (not curated studio mixtures) are the evaluation distribution.
  • Inclusivity — Vaani spans multiple Indian languages and a wide range of speakers. The eval set is monitored for language-wise and class-wise balance.
  • Transparency — Top-5 submissions must release code and document pre-trained dependencies.

数据集 — 赛道1：噪声事件检测

Vaani语料库

该数据集源自Vaani语料库——一个大规模、公开发布的印度语言语音数据集，涵盖多种印度语言，收集范围遍及印度100多个地区。

论文：arxiv.org/abs/2603.28714

训练数据 — 三个标注层级（约150小时）

训练数据以三个不同标注质量级别提供。有效利用不同质量级别标注的数据是本竞赛的关键内容。

# 标注类型 时长 描述

# Datathon@IndoML 2026 — 赛道1：噪声事件检测

## 关于本赛事

**Datathon@IndoML 2026** 是与 [IndoML 2026](https://indoml.in) 联合举办的一项研究导向型数据科学竞赛。今年的数据马拉松挑战参赛者解决**印度语言真实语音中的噪声事件检测和消除** —— 这是实现跨印度语言包容性、稳健自动语音识别的关键问题。

## 赛道1 — 检测

在印度语言语音录音中检测噪声事件，精确标注起始/终止时间戳。有效利用在不同级别（金级/银级/铜级）标注的数据来构建稳健的噪声事件检测系统。

保留的测试集（11小时）包含7小时的自然（真实）录音和4小时的合成录音（清晰语音加合成噪声）。赛道1基于全部11小时进行评分；自然/合成分解仅供透明性报告。训练数据（金级/银级/铜级共约150小时）可从Hugging Face获取：[ARTPARK-IISc/Vaani-Noise-Event-Dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/ARTPARK-IISc/Vaani-Noise-Event-Dataset)（下载代码包含其中；此赛道无需图像文件）。

在真实印度环境中收集的语音录音主要包含非平稳背景事件 —— 汽车喇叭声、狗叫声、儿童哭声、门铃声、手机铃声、厨房电器声和宗教音乐。这些事件会降低下游自动语音识别性能。

## 动机

大多数学术语音增强基准围绕平稳噪声（白噪声、粉红噪声、咖啡厅嗡鸣声）或录音棚录制的混合音频构建。来自印度农村和半城市地区的现场录音包含突发性、语义丰富的事件 —— 经过的摩托车、母鸡、高压锅哨声、门铃、另一间房间的电视 —— 当前的去噪器要么会模糊处理，要么将其视为语音。

由此产生两个后果：

- 下游自动语音识别在这些环境中的使用者身上表现失效，加剧了高资源语言和低资源印度语言之间现有的性能差距。
- 标准音频事件检测数据集（AudioSet、DESED、DCASE）代表性不足，既缺少印度声学背景，也缺少印度语言语音，使得从其迁移学习脆弱不堪。

本挑赛直接针对这一差距。它要求参赛者将噪声视为第一级、带标签、时间局部化的对象。

## 负责任AI对齐

本挑赛在负责任AI赛道下定位，基于三个明确轴线：

- **稳健性** —— 真实印度语言录音（非精心策划的录音棚混合音频）是评估分布。
- **包容性** —— Vaani涵盖多种印度语言和多种说话者。评估集按语言和类别平衡进行监控。
- **透明性** —— 前5名提交者必须公开代码并记录预训练依赖项。

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
Evaluation — Track 1: Noise Event Detection

Submission Format

Submit a ZIP file containing a single file named predictions.jsonl.

Each line of the JSONL file must be a JSON object with the following structure: 

{"clip_id": "vaani_eval_001", "events": [{"onset": 1.24, "offset": 3.81}, {"onset": 5.10, "offset": 6.55}]}
{"clip_id": "vaani_eval_002", "events": []}
{"clip_id": "vaani_eval_003", "events": [{"onset": 0.20, "offset": 0.85}, {"onset": 3.44, "offset": 4.11}]}
  • clip_id (string) — must match the clip IDs in the evaluation set.
  • events (list) — detected noise events, each with:
    • onset (float) — start time in seconds.
    • offset (float) — end time in seconds.
  • Use an empty list [] for clips with no detected noise events.
  • One JSON object per line. Every evaluation clip must appear exactly once — this includes both natural and synthetic clips in the withheld test set (11 h total: 7 h natural + 4 h synthetic).

Scoring Scope

Track 1 (Detection) is scored on the full test set — natural and synthetic clips combined. A natural/synthetic breakdown of Event F1 and Segment Dice is also reported for transparency but does not affect the leaderboard ranking.

Evaluation Metrics

1. Event-based F1 (±20% tolerance)

A predicted event is considered a true positive when both its onset and offset are within ±20% of the reference event duration (minimum 50 ms tolerance).

Formally, for a reference event with duration d = offset − onset:

  • Tolerance: tol = max(0.20 × d, 0.05) seconds
  • Match condition: |pred_onset − ref_onset| ≤ tol AND |pred_offset − ref_offset| ≤ tol

Events are matched greedily (closest first). Micro-averaged F1 is computed: 

  Precision = TP / (TP + FP)
  Recall    = TP / (TP + FN)
  F1        = 2 × Precision × Recall / (Precision + Recall)

2. Segment-level Dice Coefficient

The audio timeline is divided into 10 ms frames. For each clip, binary frame-level masks are created for both reference and predicted events. The Dice coefficient measures temporal overlap: 

  Dice = 2 × |P ∩ G| / (|P| + |G|)

where P = predicted noise frames, G = ground-truth noise frames. Macro-averaged across all evaluation clips.

Combined Score (Leaderboard Ranking)

The combined score used for leaderboard ranking is: 

  Combined = Event F1 + Segment Dice

Maximum possible: 2.0 (perfect F1 = 1.0 + perfect Dice = 1.0).

Reference Code

The snippets below reproduce exactly how the scorer computes the two metrics and how to package a valid submission. They are provided so you can validate your pipeline locally before uploading.

Building the submission ZIP

Put a single predictions.jsonl at the root of the archive (no enclosing folder). Every evaluation clip must appear exactly once: 

import json, zipfile

# predictions is a dict: clip_id -> list of (onset, offset) tuples in seconds
predictions = {
    "vaani_eval_001": [(1.24, 3.81), (5.10, 6.55)],
    "vaani_eval_002": [],
    # ...
}

with open("predictions.jsonl", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    for clip_id, events in predictions.items():
        record = {"clip_id": clip_id,
                  "events": [{"onset": on, "offset": off} for on, off in events]}
        f.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

with zipfile.ZipFile("submission.zip", "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
    z.write("predictions.jsonl", "predictions.jsonl")   # at ZIP root

Event-based F1 (±20% tolerance)

Greedy (closest-first) matching with a per-event tolerance of max(0.20 × ref_duration, 0.05) seconds, micro-averaged over all clips. 

def match_events(ref_events, pred_events, tolerance_frac=0.20):
    matched_ref, matched_pred = set(), set()
    candidates = []
    for ri, (r_on, r_off) in enumerate(ref_events):
        tol = max(tolerance_frac * (r_off - r_on), 0.05)   # at least 50 ms
        for pi, (p_on, p_off) in enumerate(pred_events):
            if abs(p_on - r_on) <= tol and abs(p_off - r_off) <= tol:
                candidates.append((abs(p_on - r_on) + abs(p_off - r_off), ri, pi))
    for _, ri, pi in sorted(candidates):        # closest first
        if ri not in matched_ref and pi not in matched_pred:
            matched_ref.add(ri); matched_pred.add(pi)
    tp = len(matched_ref)
    return tp, len(pred_events) - tp, len(ref_events) - tp   # tp, fp, fn

def event_based_f1(ref_data, pred_data):
    TP = FP = FN = 0
    for clip_id, ref_events in ref_data.items():
        tp, fp, fn = match_events(ref_events, pred_data.get(clip_id, []))
        TP += tp; FP += fp; FN += fn
    for clip_id in pred_data:                   # extra clips -> false positives
        if clip_id not in ref_data:
            FP += len(pred_data[clip_id])
    precision = TP / (TP + FP) if (TP + FP) else 0.0
    recall    = TP / (TP + FN) if (TP + FN) else 0.0
    return (2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)
            if (precision + recall) else 0.0)

Segment-level Dice

Events are rasterised to a 10 ms frame grid per clip; Dice measures temporal overlap and is macro-averaged across clips. 

def events_to_frames(events, max_time, frame_len=0.01):
    n_frames = int(max_time / frame_len) + 1
    mask = [0] * n_frames
    for on, off in events:
        for i in range(int(on / frame_len), min(int(off / frame_len) + 1, n_frames)):
            mask[i] = 1
    return mask

def segment_dice(ref_data, pred_data):
    scores = []
    for clip_id, ref_events in ref_data.items():
        pred_events = pred_data.get(clip_id, [])
        all_events = ref_events + pred_events
        if not all_events:
            scores.append(1.0); continue
        max_time = max(off for _, off in all_events) + 0.5   # pad 0.5 s
        ref_mask  = events_to_frames(ref_events,  max_time)
        pred_mask = events_to_frames(pred_events, max_time)
        inter = sum(r & p for r, p in zip(ref_mask, pred_mask))
        total = sum(ref_mask) + sum(pred_mask)
        scores.append(1.0 if total == 0 else 2.0 * inter / total)
    return sum(scores) / len(scores) if scores else 0.0

Novelty Score

Following metric-based ranking, an expert panel applies a novelty factor to the top-5 entries to determine the final standings. This rewards original contributions: new architectures, novel training regimes, principled event-conditioning, or semi-supervised approaches exploiting unlabelled Vaani audio.

Submission Limits

Max submissions per day5
Max total submissions100
Execution time limit600 seconds

评估 — 赛道 1：噪音事件检测

提交格式

提交一个包含单个文件 predictions.jsonl 的 ZIP 文件。

JSONL 文件的每一行必须是具有以下结构的 JSON 对象： 

{"clip_id": "vaani_eval_001", "events": [{"onset": 1.24, "offset": 3.81}, {"onset": 5.10, "offset": 6.55}]}
{"clip_id": "vaani_eval_002", "events": []}
{"clip_id": "vaani_eval_003", "events": [{"onset": 0.20, "offset": 0.85}, {"onset": 3.44, "offset": 4.11}]}
  • clip_id（字符串）— 必须与评估集中的片段 ID 匹配。
  • events（列表）— 检测到的噪音事件，每个包含：
    • onset（浮点数）— 开始时间（秒）。
    • offset（浮点数）— 结束时间（秒）。
  • 对于没有检测到噪音事件的片段，使用空列表 []。
  • 每行一个 JSON 对象。每个评估片段必须恰好出现一次 — 这包括隐藏测试集中的自然和合成片段（总共 11 小时：7 小时自然 + 4 小时合成）。

评分范围

赛道 1（检测）在完整测试集上评分 — 自然和合成片段合并。还会报告事件 F1 和分段 Dice 系数的自然/合成分组结果以供参考，但不影响排行榜排名。

评估指标

1. 基于事件的 F1（±20% 容差）

当预测事件的开始时间和结束时间都在参考事件持续时间的 ±20% 范围内（最小 50 ms 容差）时，该预测事件被视为真正例。

形式上，对于持续时间为 d = offset − onset 的参考事件：

  • 容差：tol = max(0.20 × d, 0.05) 秒
  • 匹配条件：|pred_onset − ref_onset| ≤ tol 且 |pred_offset − ref_offset| ≤ tol

事件按贪心匹配（最接近的优先）。计算微观平均 F1： 

  精准率 = TP / (TP + FP)
  召回率 = TP / (TP + FN)
  F1    = 2 × 精准率 × 召回率 / (精准率 + 召回率)

2. 分段级 Dice 系数

音频时间轴被分为 10 ms 的帧。对于每个片段，为参考和预测事件创建二进制帧级掩码。Dice 系数衡量时间重叠： 

  Dice = 2 × |P ∩ G| / (|P| + |G|)

其中 P = 预测的噪音帧，G = 地面真实噪音帧。 在所有评估片段上进行宏观平均。

综合得分（排行榜排名）

用于排行榜排名的综合得分为： 

  综合 = 事件 F1 + 分段 Dice

最高可能值：2.0（完美 F1 = 1.0 + 完美 Dice = 1.0）。

创新性得分

在基于指标排名后，专家评审团对前 5 个参赛作品应用创新性因子以确定最终排名。这奖励原创贡献：新的架构、新颖的训练方案、原理性的事件条件设置或利用未标注 Vaani 音频的半监督方法。

提交限制

每天最大提交次数5
最大总提交次数100
执行时间限制600 秒

UPAR Challenge Track 2: Attribute-based Person Retrieval

## News - Oct 8, 2026: Update from CPU to GPU runners: Nvidia A10 GPU, 24 GB VRAM, 20 CPU Cores, 40 GB RAM, time limit per run: 5 minutes - Oct 6, 2026: We have clarified the rules concerning post-processing and re-ranking. Please review them to ensure compliance. - Oct 2, 2026: New code & fact sheet submission deadline: **Oct 26, 2026, AoE**. Due to strict WACV deadlines, we must move up the d - eadline. - Sep 30, 2026: [Track3](https://www.codabench.org/competitions/18273/) on Human Pose Estimation is now live ## Challenge & Workshop Track 1 of the **UPAR Challenge** at the Real-World Surveillance workshop (RWS), WACV 2027. Everything about this track lives on this Codabench page: task, data, evaluation, submission format, schedule and rules. Announcements go out by email to registered participants. See also the workshop website and Tasks 2 and 3 of the UPAR Challenge. The RWS workshop welcomes both regular submissions on the topic of real-world surveillance and submissions as part of the Challenge: - [RWS Workshop](https://vap.aau.dk/rws/) - [Challenge Task 1: Pedestrian Attribute Recognition](https://www.codabench.org/competitions/18180/) - [Challenge Task 2: Attribute-Based Person Retrieval](https://www.codabench.org/competitions/18196/) - [Challenge Task 3: Human Pose Estimation](https://www.codabench.org/competitions/18273/) ## The task Find people by description. A query is not an image but a **set of attributes**, such as *adult, female, long hair, red short-sleeved top, black trousers, backpack*. For every query, rank a gallery of pedestrian images so that the people matching the description come first. Queries use the 40 binary UPAR attributes: age, gender, hair length, upper and lower body clothing length, colour and type, and accessories. The challenge builds on the UPAR dataset, which unifies the annotations of several public pedestrian datasets. The gallery comes from a hidden domain your model has never seen, so the method has to generalize. You submit **code, not rankings**. Your model runs inside the evaluation container on a hidden gallery, and only the resulting metrics are published. ## Getting started 1. Read the **Data** page and download the training data and example submission. [Starter Kit](https://github.com/speckean/UPAR-Challenge-2027) 2. Take the **example submission** as your template. It shows the functions the platform calls. 3. Put your model and weights into the submission folder, zip the **contents** of the folder so `run.py` is at the archive root, and upload it under **My Submissions**. See the **Submission** page for the API your `run.py` must expose, and the **Evaluation** page for the metrics. Submissions run in `pytorch/pytorch:2.4.1-cuda12.1-cudnn9-runtime` (Python 3.11, torch 2.4.1, torchvision, numpy, Pillow) with **no network access**. Ship everything your model needs inside the zip. ## Code submission and winner selection After the challenge deadline, participating teams are required to submit their code, models, and a short description of their method (fact sheet) by **Oct 26, 2026, AoE** to **upar.challenge@gmail.com**. A panel of experts will review the entries. The executable/source code should include trained models, training code, and necessary parameters to ensure reproducibility. Teams that do not comply are removed from the final ranking. Note: Submitted codes will not be saved on the evaluation servers. Final submission codebases provided to the organizers will be used only for reproducibility checks and winner verification, and will not be shared publicly or with other participants at any stage. ## Paper submission We strongly encourage all challenge participants to submit a technical paper to the RWS workshop. # Data

## Training data

Training data and starter kit can be found here: [Starter Kit](https://github.com/speckean/UPAR-Challenge-2027)
The use of external data to fine-tune PAR is not permitted.
Pre-trained models trained on common datasets such as ImageNet, or foundation models/VLMs that were not specifically trained for PAR, are permitted.

## Attributes

40 binary attributes, in this exact order. A query is a vector of 40 values,
`1` = the person has the attribute, `0` = the person does not.

```text
 0 Age-Young                  20 LowerBody-Length-Short
 1 Age-Adult                  21 LowerBody-Color-Black
 2 Age-Old                    22 LowerBody-Color-Blue
 3 Gender-Female              23 LowerBody-Color-Brown
 4 Hair-Length-Short          24 LowerBody-Color-Green
 5 Hair-Length-Long           25 LowerBody-Color-Grey
 6 Hair-Length-Bald           26 LowerBody-Color-Orange
 7 UpperBody-Length-Short     27 LowerBody-Color-Pink
 8 UpperBody-Color-Black      28 LowerBody-Color-Purple
 9 UpperBody-Color-Blue       29 LowerBody-Color-Red
10 UpperBody-Color-Brown      30 LowerBody-Color-White
11 UpperBody-Color-Green      31 LowerBody-Color-Yellow
12 UpperBody-Color-Grey       32 LowerBody-Color-Other
13 UpperBody-Color-Orange     33 LowerBody-Type-Trousers&Shorts
14 UpperBody-Color-Pink       34 LowerBody-Type-Skirt&Dress
15 UpperBody-Color-Purple     35 Accessory-Backpack
16 UpperBody-Color-Red        36 Accessory-Bag
17 UpperBody-Color-White      37 Accessory-Glasses-Normal
18 UpperBody-Color-Yellow     38 Accessory-Glasses-Sun
19 UpperBody-Color-Other      39 Accessory-Hat
```

## Test data

The test set is hidden. It is mounted into your container, read-only, with this
layout:

```text
input_data/
├── queries.csv     one query per line: 40 comma-separated 0/1 values
├── images.csv      the gallery: one image path per line, no labels
├── images/         the image files, at the paths listed in images.csv
│   └── <dataset>/...
└── task.json       attribute names, number of queries and gallery images
```

The queries are complete descriptions: every query is the full attribute
vector of at least one person in the gallery. A gallery image is a **correct
match** for a query if all 40 of its attributes equal the query. Several
images can match the same query, and an image never matches two queries.

The gallery images are pedestrian crops of varying size and aspect ratio.

You do not have to parse these files yourself: the ingestion program does it
and hands your code the queries and the gallery in one `sample` dict. See the
**Submission** page.

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
# Evaluation

The protocol and metrics are those of the previous UPAR challenge edition
(WACV 2024). The scoring program reproduces the original evaluation script.

## What is evaluated

For every query your model returns a ranking of the **whole gallery**, best
match first. A gallery image is a correct match for a query if all of its 40
attributes equal the query.

## Metrics

| Leaderboard | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **mADM** | mean average degree of match - **the ranking metric** |
| mAP | mean average precision over the queries |
| Rank-1 | share of queries whose top result is a correct match |
| Rank-5 | share of queries with a correct match among the top 5 |
| Rank-10 | share of queries with a correct match among the top 10 |
| mINP | mean inverse negative penalty |

For one query with `R` correct matches in the gallery, at the ranks
`r_1 < r_2 < ... < r_R` of your ranking:

```text
AP  = ( 1/r_1 + 2/r_2 + ... + R/r_R ) / R
INP = R / r_R
```

`AP` rewards placing **all** correct matches early. `INP` looks only at the
hardest one: it is 1 if the last correct match directly follows the others,
and falls towards 0 the deeper you have to search for it. `mAP` and `mINP` are
the means over the queries, `Rank-k` is the share of queries with `r_1 <= k`.

### mADM - the ranking metric

`AP` is all-or-nothing: an image that differs from the query in a single
attribute counts exactly like one that differs in twenty. The **average degree
of match** (ADM) keeps the structure of `AP` but credits near misses.

For a query, the degree of match of a gallery image is the share of the 40
attributes on which image and query agree. It is normalized per query, so that
an average gallery image earns nothing and a perfect match earns 1:

```text
dom(g)  = (number of attributes where image g equals the query) / 40
ndom(g) = max( 0, (dom(g) - mean dom) / (max dom - mean dom) )      mean, max over the gallery
```

With `g_1, g_2, ...` your ranking and `r_1 < ... < r_R` again the ranks of the
correct matches:

```text
ADM = ( 1/R ) * sum over k of  ( ndom(g_1) + ... + ndom(g_{r_k}) ) / r_k
```

So at the rank of every correct match, `AP` asks *which share of the images
ranked so far is correct*, and `ADM` asks *how well do the images ranked so far
match the query on average*. A ranking that places similar-looking people
ahead of unrelated ones scores higher than one that does not, even if both
find the exact matches at the same ranks. A perfect ranking reaches 1. `mADM`
is the mean over the queries.

Reference: A. Specker, J. Beyerer, *Balanced Pedestrian Attribute Recognition
for Improved Attribute-based Person Retrieval*, 2023, and the UPAR Challenge
2024 report.

## Ties

If you return distances or similarities, equal values are ranked in gallery
order. Avoid large groups of ties, they make your result depend on that order.

## Leaderboard

Your **latest** submission is the one shown on the leaderboard, not your best.
pages.content_zh:
# 评估

协议和指标采用前一届UPAR挑战赛版本（WACV 2024）的标准。评分程序复现了原始评估脚本。

## 评估内容

对于每个查询，你的模型需要返回整个库集的排名，最佳匹配排在首位。如果库集图像的所有40个属性都与查询相等，则该图像是查询的正确匹配。

## 指标

| 排行榜 | 含义 |
| --- | --- |
| **mADM** | 平均匹配度 - **排名指标** |
| mAP | 查询的平均精度均值 |
| Rank-1 | 最高排名结果是正确匹配的查询占比 |
| Rank-5 | 前5个结果中包含正确匹配的查询占比 |
| Rank-10 | 前10个结果中包含正确匹配的查询占比 |
| mINP | 平均逆负惩罚 |

对于一个查询，库集中有`R`个正确匹配，其排名为`r_1 < r_2 < ... < r_R`：

```text
AP  = ( 1/r_1 + 2/r_2 + ... + R/r_R ) / R
INP = R / r_R
```

`AP`奖励**所有**正确匹配都排在前面的情况。`INP`仅关注最难找到的匹配：如果最后一个正确匹配紧接在其他匹配之后则为1，搜索深度越深则数值越接近0。`mAP`和`mINP`是所有查询的均值，`Rank-k`是`r_1 <= k`的查询占比。

### mADM - 排名指标

`AP`是全有或全无的：与查询相差一个属性的图像与相差二十个属性的图像计数完全相同。**平均匹配度**（ADM）保持`AP`的结构但对接近匹配进行评分。

对于一个查询，库集图像的匹配度是该图像与查询相同的40个属性的占比。它按查询进行归一化，使得平均库集图像获得0分，完美匹配获得1分：

```text
dom(g)  = (图像g与查询相同的属性数) / 40
ndom(g) = max( 0, (dom(g) - 平均dom) / (最大dom - 平均dom) )      平均值、最大值取遍整个库集
```

对于排名`g_1, g_2, ...`和正确匹配的排名`r_1 < ... < r_R`：

```text
ADM = ( 1/R ) * 对k求和  ( ndom(g_1) + ... + ndom(g_{r_k}) ) / r_k
```

因此，在每个正确匹配的排名位置，`AP`问的是**到目前为止排名的图像中有多少比例是正确的**，而`ADM`问的是**到目前为止排名的图像平均匹配度如何**。将外观相似的人排在无关人员之前的排名得分更高，即使两者都在相同位置找到精确匹配也是如此。完美排名达到1分。`mADM`是所有查询的均值。

参考文献：A. Specker, J. Beyerer, *Balanced Pedestrian Attribute Recognition for Improved Attribute-based Person Retrieval*, 2023，以及UPAR挑战赛2024报告。

## 平局

如果返回距离或相似性，相等值按库集顺序排名。避免大量平局组，它们会使结果依赖于该顺序。

## 排行榜

排行榜显示的是你的**最新**提交，而非最佳提交。

# Submission

You upload a zip containing your model, the platform runs it against data you never see.

## The zip

Zip the **contents** of your submission folder, not the folder itself:

```bash
cd my_submission
zip -r ../my_submission.zip . -x "*/__pycache__/*" "*.DS_Store" ".git/*"
unzip -l ../my_submission.zip | head    # run.py must be at the root
```

Required at the root of the archive:

```text
run.py           your entry point
metadata.yaml    copy it unchanged from the example submission
<anything else>  weights, modules, configs
```

## The API

The ingestion program imports `run.py` and calls:

```python
def load_model() -> None:
    """Optional. Called once. Load your weights here."""

def rank_gallery(sample: dict) -> dict:
    """Called once, with all queries and the whole gallery."""
```

`sample` is:

```python
{
  "attribute_names": ["Age-Young", "Age-Adult", ...],     # the 40 names, in order
  "queries": [[0, 1, 0, 1, ...], ...],                    # Q queries x 40 values (0/1)
  "gallery": [                                            # G gallery images
    {"index": 0,
     "image": "<dataset>/images/0.jpg",                       # path as listed in images.csv
     "image_path": "/app/input_data/images/<dataset>/images/0.jpg"},   # absolute, readable
    ...
  ],
}
```

Return a dict with **exactly one** of these keys. Each holds a `Q x G` matrix
(list of lists, numpy array or tensor): row `i` belongs to `queries[i]`,
column `j` to `gallery[j]`.

| Key | Content | Ranked |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"distances"` | float, how far image `j` is from query `i` | smallest first |
| `"similarities"` | float, how well image `j` matches query `i` | largest first |
| `"ranking"` | int, row `i` = all gallery indices `0..G-1`, best match first | as given |

The key states the direction of your values, so a distance is never mistaken
for a score. A bare array, NaN/Inf, a wrong shape, or a `ranking` row that is
not a permutation of `0..G-1` fail the submission with a message in the
ingestion log. Equal distances or similarities are ranked in gallery order.

The usual recipe is two steps: predict attribute probabilities for every
gallery image once, then compute the distance of every query to every image.
The example submission does exactly that, without ever building a
`Q x G x 40` tensor.

## Runtime environment

- **No network access.** Ship your weights inside the zip. Nothing is downloaded at run time.
- The image is `pytorch/pytorch:2.4.1-cuda12.1-cudnn9-runtime`: Python 3.11,
  torch 2.4.1, torchvision, numpy, Pillow. Anything else your code imports must
  travel in the zip.
- There is a wall-clock limit for the whole run. `rank_gallery()` is a single
  call, so batch your image loading and inference yourself, and print your own
  progress: it shows up in the ingestion log.
- The working directory is your submission folder, so relative paths to your
  weights work.

# 提交

您上传一个zip文件，平台使用您未曾看过的数据对其进行测试。

## Zip文件

压缩您提交文件夹的**内容**，而非文件夹本身：

```bash
cd my_submission
zip -r ../my_submission.zip . -x "*/__pycache__/*" "*.DS_Store" ".git/*"
unzip -l ../my_submission.zip | head    # run.py 必须在根目录
```

归档文件根目录需要的文件：

```text

metadata.yaml    从示例提交中原样复制
<其他任何文件>   权重、模块、配置
```

## API

摄取程序导入 `run.py` 并调用：

```python
def load_model() -> None:
    """可选。调用一次。在此处加载您的权重。"""

def rank_gallery(sample: dict) -> dict:
    """调用一次，包含所有查询和整个库。"""
```

`sample` 结构为：

```python
{
  "attribute_names": ["Age-Young", "Age-Adult", ...],     # 40个名称，按顺序
  "queries": [[0, 1, 0, 1, ...], ...],                    # Q个查询 x 40个值 (0/1)
  "gallery": [                                            # G个库图像
    {"index": 0,
     "image": "<dataset>/images/0.jpg",                       # images.csv中列出的路径
     "image_path": "/app/input_data/images/<dataset>/images/0.jpg"},   # 绝对路径，可读
    ...
  ],
}
```

返回一个字典，**恰好包含以下键之一**。每个键对应一个 `Q x G` 矩阵（列表嵌套、numpy数组或张量）：第 `i` 行对应 `queries[i]`，第 `j` 列对应 `gallery[j]`。

| 键 | 内容 | 排序方式 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"distances"` | 浮点数，图像 `j` 与查询 `i` 的距离 | 从小到大 |
| `"similarities"` | 浮点数，图像 `j` 与查询 `i` 的匹配程度 | 从大到小 |
| `"ranking"` | 整数，第 `i` 行 = 所有库索引 `0..G-1`，最佳匹配优先 | 按给定顺序 |

该键说明了您的值的方向，因此距离不会被误认为是得分。裸数组、NaN/Inf、错误形状或 `ranking` 行不是 `0..G-1` 的排列都会导致提交失败，并在摄取日志中显示错误信息。相等的距离或相似性按库顺序排名。

通常的做法分两步：预测每个库图像的属性概率（仅一次），然后计算每个查询到每个图像的距离。示例提交正是这样做的，无需构建 `Q x G x 40` 张量。

## 运行时环境

- **无网络访问。** 在zip中包含您的权重。运行时不下载任何内容。
- 镜像为 `pytorch/pytorch:2.4.1-cuda12.1-cudnn9-runtime`：Python 3.11、torch 2.4.1、torchvision、numpy、Pillow。您的代码导入的任何其他内容必须包含在zip中。
- 整个运行有时间限制。`rank_gallery()` 是单次调用，因此请自行批量加载图像和推理，并打印您自己的进度：这会显示在摄取日志中。
- 工作目录是您的提交文件夹，因此相对路径指向您的权重是可行的。

pages.title: Overview
pages.content:
# LongVQU-Eval Challenge

**Evaluating Long-Term Video Quality Understanding of Large Vision-Language Models**

IEEE Signal Processing Society Challenge 2026

## Motivation

Traditional video quality assessment (VMAF, SSIM, PSNR, NR-VQA models) works well on
short clips but cannot reason over long temporal context and accumulate perceptual
degradations evidence across events.
**LongVQU-Eval Challenge** aims to close this gap with a multiple-choice question-answering assessment built on
[LongVQUBench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Aarna004/LongVQUBench). 

## Hierarchical evaluation

| Level | Name | What models must do |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **LQU** — Local Event Quality Understanding | Detect, localize, classify, and rate the severity of isolated distortion events |
| 2 | **CQR** — Cross-Event Quality Reasoning | Compare and integrate perceptual evidence across multiple distortion events |
| 3 | **GQU** — Global Quality Understanding | Synthesize a holistic quality judgment over the full video |

Within each level, questions are further grouped by `qa_category`
(e.g. Comparison, Cumulative Effect) and `question_type`
(yes-or-no, what, which, how).

## How the challenge works

- **Videos:** Development Phase videos are on
  Hugging Face (`Aarna004/LongVQUBench`, `grouped_tars/<LEVEL>/<Category>/*.tar`);
  Test Phase videos are a separate, currently-unpublished. Please check Data & Submission Format for details.
- **Questions live on Codabench :**  Each phase publishes a `questions.json`
  with the video reference, the question, and its multiple-choice options.
- **Build your model :** Offline (on your own compute)
- **Submit only your predictions :**  CSV format (`question_idx, predicted_option`). 
  See the Data & Submission Format page for the exact format.

Scoring is exact-match accuracy against the hidden ground truth, with no
constraints on your model, framework, or inference setup **(Proprietary,
paid-API-only models are not eligible).**

## Who can participate

Individuals or teams of 1-5. Both academic and industry participants are
welcome.



## Organizers

Hanwei Zhu : hanwei.zhu@ntu.edu.sg

Nanyang Technological University, Singapore

# LongVQU-Eval 挑战赛

**评估大型视觉语言模型的长期视频质量理解能力**

IEEE信号处理协会挑战赛 2026

## 动机

传统视频质量评估方法（VMAF、SSIM、PSNR、NR-VQA模型）在短视频上表现良好，但无法在长时间上下文上进行推理，也无法跨事件累积感知退化证据。
**LongVQU-Eval挑战赛**旨在通过构建在[LongVQUBench](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Aarna004/LongVQUBench)基础上的多选问答评估来弥补这一差距。

## 分层评估

| 级别 | 名称 | 模型需要完成的任务 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **LQU** — 局部事件质量理解 | 检测、定位、分类和评定孤立失真事件的严重程度 |
| 2 | **CQR** — 跨事件质量推理 | 比较和整合多个失真事件的感知证据 |
| 3 | **GQU** — 全局质量理解 | 对完整视频进行整体质量判断 |

在每个级别内，问题进一步按`qa_category`（如对比、累积效果）和`question_type`（是/否、什么、哪个、如何）分组。

## 挑战赛运作流程

- **视频：** 开发阶段视频位于Hugging Face（`Aarna004/LongVQUBench`、`grouped_tars/<LEVEL>/<Category>/*.tar`）；测试阶段视频为独立的未公开数据集。请查看数据和提交格式页面了解详情。
- **问题发布在Codabench上：** 每个阶段发布一个`questions.json`文件，包含视频参考、问题和多选选项。
- **构建您的模型：** 离线方式（在您自己的计算环境上）
- **仅提交预测结果：** CSV格式（`question_idx, predicted_option`）。详见数据和提交格式页面的准确格式。

评分为与隐藏真值的完全匹配准确度，对您的模型、框架或推理设置**没有限制**（不允许仅限专有和付费API的模型）。

## 参赛资格

1-5人的个人或团队。欢迎学术和行业参与者。

# Data & Submission Format

## Data Batches

| Batch | Size | Videos | Answers public? | Where |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Development (Train)** | 1,200 MCQs | on Hugging Face now | Yes | Codabench `public_data/train/questions.json` (WITH `answer`/`answer_idx`) |
| **Test** | TBA | TBA | No, until challenge ends | Codabench `public_data/test_public/questions.json` (candidates only) |

These are two **independent** annotation batches with non-overlapping
`question_idx` values. The Train batch's answers are public (it's on the
gated Hugging Face repo, so anyone with Hub access can see them). Please treat
any Dev-phase leaderboard score as your pipeline check. The **Test batch determines the final ranking**.

## Where the data lives

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Train videos | Hugging Face: [`Aarna004/LongVQUBench`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Aarna004/LongVQUBench) — `grouped_tars/<LEVEL>/<Category>/*.tar`. Requires accepting the dataset's terms + a Hub login. |
| Test videos | **TBD — to be announced on 15 Oct 2026.** <This row will be replaced with the  link>. |
| Train questions **with answers** | Codabench, Development Phase `public_data/train/questions.json` |
| Test questions **without answers** | Codabench, Test Phase `public_data/test_public/questions.json` |



## `questions.json` schema

One entry per question:

```json
{
  "question_idx": 246,
  "video_idx": 1212,
  "hierarchy_category": "CQR",
  "question_type": "yes-or-no",
  "qa_category": "Comparison",
  "question": "Is the perceptual degradation in the first 30 seconds more severe than that between 138.37s and 153.35s?",
  "candidates": ["Yes", "No"],
  "answer": "No",
  "answer_idx": 2
}
```

- `hierarchy_category`: `"LQU"` | `"CQR"` | `"GQU"`
- `candidates`: 2–4 answer options
- `answer` / `answer_idx`: **present in the Development Phase file only.**
  The Test Phase file omits both — you're scored against a hidden copy.
- `video_idx`: matches the video's identifier inside the Hugging Face
  `grouped_tars` archives — use this to locate the right video.

## What you submit

A single **`predictions.csv`** at the root of your submission zip:

```csv
question_idx,predicted_option
246,4
422,2
469,3
```

`predicted_option` is the **1-based index** into that question's
`candidates` array (e.g. answering `"No"` for
`["Yes", "No"]` → `predicted_option = 2`).



**Unanswered `question_idx` values are scored as incorrect, so partial
submissions are allowed but will lower your accuracy.**

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
# Evaluation

## Metric

**Accuracy**: Exact match between your `predicted_option` and the hidden
`answer_idx`, averaged over all questions in the phase. Unanswered
questions count as incorrect.

The leaderboard also reports accuracy broken out per hierarchy level
(LQU / CQR / GQU) for diagnostic purposes, and the number of questions you
provided an answer for (`# Answered`), but ranking is by **Overall
Accuracy**.

## Leaderboard columns

| Column | Key | Sort |
|---|---|---|
| Overall Accuracy | `accuracy` | desc |
| LQU Accuracy | `lqu_accuracy` | desc |
| CQR Accuracy | `cqr_accuracy` | desc |
| GQU Accuracy | `gqu_accuracy` | desc |
| # Answered | `num_answered` | desc |

Ranking uses `accuracy` as the primary sort key. Ties are broken, in order, by:

1. **Inference time** (lower is better), as reported in the submitted methodology document
2. **Parameter count** (lower is better), as reported in the submitted methodology document

## Submission rule

Each phase uses `Force_Last`: only your most recent successful submission
counts toward your leaderboard position, so resubmitting simply replaces
your prior score rather than stacking multiple ranked entries.

Individuals or teams of **1-5 participants**. Both academic and industry

pages.title: Overview
pages.content: # RoboWorld 2026 Track 1: WorldNav Welcome to WorldNav, the language-conditioned visual navigation track of the RoboWorld 2026, affiliated with the RoboPAD Workshop at NeurIPS 2026. An agent receives one initial egocentric RGB image and a natural-language instruction. It must predict a complete navigation action sequence without a goal image, an initial numeric pose, or further observations from the environment. World models, vision-language-action models, and policy-only methods are welcome. ## Task Definition Submit variable-length sequences of `[dx, dy, dyaw]` actions. `dx` means forward motion and `dy` means leftward motion in the agent's current local frame; `dyaw` changes heading in radians. The private evaluator uses the recorded initial pose to reconstruct the predicted route. Test participants receive only the initial image and instruction, not the pose, goal, reference trajectory, or reference action sequence. ## Phases Phase 1 is for development and validation. pages.content:
# Submission & Evaluation

Submit predicted action sequences in a ZIP archive, using only each episode's initial RGB image and instruction.

## Action format

Each action is [dx, dy, dyaw]: forward displacement, leftward displacement in the agent's **current local frame**, and yaw update in radians. Sequences may have different lengths; the JSON list ends the trajectory.


Limits: at most 64 actions per episode; hypot(dx,dy) ≤ 2.46 dataset coordinate units and |dyaw| ≤ 6.29 rad per action (evaluated modulo 2π in [−π, π)).

## ZIP layout

Put the required JSON files at the archive root. The downloadable example ZIP shows the layout and Phase 1 episode IDs; replace its illustrative actions.

| Phase |   | Required files |
| :-- | :--: | :-- |
| Phase 1 |   | val_seen.json, val_unseen.json |
| Phase 2 |   | test.json |

### JSON schema

Each file contains split and episodes. Include every phase episode_id exactly once, with an actions list:

    {
      "split": "val_unseen",
      "episodes": [
        {
          "episode_id": "20210826_40_0001_02_0",
          "actions": [[0.25, 0.0, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0, 0.15], [0.12, -0.05, 0.0]]
        }
      ]
    }

This abbreviated example is not a complete submission.

## Evaluation metrics

The two fidelity metrics range from 0 to 1. See [demonstration.py](https://github.com/F1y1113/worldnav-challenge/blob/main/demonstration.py) for the five calculations.

| Metric |   | Direction |   | Meaning |
| :-- | :--: | :-- | :--: | :-- |
| **Success Rate (SR)** |   | Higher |   | Fraction meeting the final-position success criterion. |
| **Absolute Trajectory Error (ATE)** |   | Lower |   | Position error over the reference trajectory. |
| **Relative Pose Error (RPE)** |   | Lower |   | Relative translation error between consecutive poses. |
| **Full-route fidelity** |   | Higher |   | Agreement with the complete ordered recorded route, including a penalty for unnecessary travel. |
| **Heading and turn fidelity** |   | Higher |   | Agreement of facing direction while moving and of the direction, position, and amount of turns. |

## Composite Score

Each episode is scored first, then the contributions are averaged:

    Score = (100/N) × Σ_i { FullRouteFidelity_i × (1 + HeadingTurnFidelity_i)/2
                          × [0.70 + 0.10 SR_i + 0.10/(1+ATE_i) + 0.10/(1+RPE_i)] }

SR_i is binary success; ATE_i and RPE_i are per-episode errors in dataset coordinate units. Score averages episode contributions.

Phase 1 ranks by `(Score_val_seen + Score_val_unseen) / 2`, with equal weight for each split. Both split files are required; a submission missing either file is rejected. Both split Scores are displayed. Phase 2 ranks by test Score.

# 提交与评估

将预测的动作序列提交至ZIP压缩包，仅使用每个片段的初始RGB图像和指令。

## 动作格式

每个动作为[dx, dy, dyaw]：前向位移、智能体**当前局部坐标系**中的左向位移，以及偏航角更新（弧度制）。序列长度可不同；JSON列表标记轨迹结束。

限制：每个片段最多64个动作；单次动作的hypot(dx,dy) ≤ 2.46数据集坐标单位且|dyaw| ≤ 6.29弧度（在[−π, π)范围内对2π取模计算）。

## ZIP文件结构

将所需的JSON文件置于压缩包根目录。可下载的示例ZIP展示了文件结构和第一阶段片段ID；替换其中的示例动作。

| 阶段 |   | 所需文件 |
| :-- | :--: | :-- |
| 第一阶段 |   | val_seen.json, val_unseen.json |
| 第二阶段 |   | test.json |

### JSON模式

每个文件包含数据集划分和片段。每个阶段的episode_id必须且只能出现一次，附带动作列表：

    {
      "split": "val_unseen",
      "episodes": [
        {
          "episode_id": "20210826_40_0001_02_0",
          "actions": [[0.25, 0.0, 0.0], [0.0, 0.0, 0.15], [0.12, -0.05, 0.0]]
        }
      ]
    }

此简化示例并非完整提交。

## 评估指标

两个保真度指标范围为0到1。五种计算方法参见[demonstration.py](https://github.com/F1y1113/worldnav-challenge/blob/main/demonstration.py)。

| 指标 |   | 方向 |   | 含义 |
| :-- | :--: | :-- | :--: | :-- |
| **成功率 (SR)** |   | 越高越好 |   | 满足最终位置成功标准的比例。 |
| **绝对轨迹误差 (ATE)** |   | 越低越好 |   | 相对于参考轨迹的位置误差。 |
| **相对位姿误差 (RPE)** |   | 越低越好 |   | 连续位姿之间的相对平移误差。 |
| **全路径保真度** |   | 越高越好 |   | 与完整有序记录路径的一致性，包括对不必要移动的惩罚。 |
| **航向与转向保真度** |   | 越高越好 |   | 移动时朝向以及转向方向、位置和幅度的一致性。 |

## 综合得分

首先对每个片段进行评分，然后取平均值：

    Score = (100/N) × Σ_i { FullRouteFidelity_i × (1 + HeadingTurnFidelity_i)/2
                          × [0.70 + 0.10 SR_i + 0.10/(1+ATE_i) + 0.10/(1+RPE_i)] }

SR_i为二元成功标志；ATE_i和RPE_i为每个片段在数据集坐标单位下的误差。得分取各片段贡献的平均值。

第一阶段按`(Score_val_seen + Score_val_unseen) / 2`排名，两个划分权重相等。两个划分的文件都必须提交；缺少任一文件的提交将被拒绝。两个划分的得分均会显示。第二阶段按测试集得分排名。

pages.content:
# Machine-oriented Image Quality Assessment (MoIQA) Challenge

Welcome to the **Machine-oriented Image Quality Assessment (MoIQA) Challenge**! This is the **2nd** MoIQA Challenge, affiliated to the **IEEE SPS Challenge Program**. The competition focuses on the machine-oriented perceptual quality of visual media.

## Background

With the development of Embodied AI, machines have replaced humans as the main consumers of visual media, yet existing Image Quality Assessment (IQA) metrics remain focused on humans and overlook machine task utility. To address this gap, we introduce the Machine-oriented Image Quality Assessment (MoIQA) Challenge. This challenge aims to advance reliable image understanding for machine preference and support robust Embodied AI applications.

---

## The Challenge

The dataset covers three major types of visual media: **AI-Generated Images (AIGI)**, **Natural Scene Images (NSI)**, and **Screen Content Images (SCI)**. In total, the dataset contains **100 reference images** and **3,000 distorted images**, where each distorted image is generated from one reference image by applying one of **30 distortion types (T01–T30)** at one of **5 severity levels (S1–S5)**.

Participants are asked to predict a **quality score** for each distorted image. The ground-truth quality scores are annotated on a **1–5 scale**, reflecting the machine-oriented perceptual quality of the visual content. The training set is released **with** ground-truth labels, while the validation and test sets are released **without** labels — participants submit their predictions to the CodaBench platform for evaluation.

---

## Competition Phases

### Development Phase
* **Objective**: Train and refine your model on the released training set (with ground-truth quality labels and reference images), and predict the quality scores of the validation set (released without labels or reference images). Predictions are submitted to CodaBench for live ranking.

### Test Phase
* **Objective**: Predict the quality scores of the held-out test set (released without labels or reference images). The final ranking is based on this phase. For both phases, prediction is performed directly on the distorted images, and submissions may be **continuous scores** — integer ratings are not required.

---

## Evaluation

Submissions are evaluated by the correlation between the predicted quality scores and the ground truth:

* **Pearson Linear Correlation Coefficient (PLCC)**: Measures the linear relationship between the predicted scores and the ground truth.
* **Spearman Rank-Order Correlation Coefficient (SRCC)**: Measures the monotonic relationship (ranking consistency) between the predicted scores and the ground truth.

The final ranking score is the **mean of PLCC and SRCC**, which is the only column shown on the leaderboard.

---

## Contact

For any inquiries, please reach out to:

* **Email**: lcysyzxdxc@sjtu.edu.cn

# 机器导向的图像质量评估（MoIQA）挑战赛

欢迎参加**机器导向的图像质量评估（MoIQA）挑战赛**！这是**第2届** MoIQA挑战赛，隶属于**IEEE SPS挑战赛项目**。该竞赛聚焦于视觉媒体的机器导向感知质量。

## 背景

随着具身人工智能的发展，机器已取代人类成为视觉媒体的主要消费者，但现有的图像质量评估（IQA）指标仍然专注于人类，忽视了机器任务效用。为了解决这一问题，我们推出了机器导向的图像质量评估（MoIQA）挑战赛。该挑战赛旨在推进机器偏好的可靠图像理解，支持稳健的具身人工智能应用。

---

## 挑战赛内容

数据集涵盖三种主要类型的视觉媒体：**AI生成图像（AIGI）**、**自然场景图像（NSI）**和**屏幕内容图像（SCI）**。数据集总共包含**100张参考图像**和**3,000张失真图像**，每张失真图像由一张参考图像通过应用**30种失真类型（T01–T30）**中的一种在**5个严重程度等级（S1–S5）**中的一个生成。

参与者需要为每张失真图像预测一个**质量分数**。基准真值质量分数在**1–5分级**上标注，反映视觉内容的机器导向感知质量。训练集发布**时包含**基准真值标签，而验证集和测试集发布**时不包含**标签——参与者将预测结果提交到CodaBench平台进行评估。

---

## 竞赛阶段

### 开发阶段
* **目标**：在发布的训练集（包含基准真值质量标签和参考图像）上训练和优化模型，并预测验证集的质量分数（发布时不包含标签或参考图像）。预测结果提交到CodaBench进行实时排名。

### 测试阶段
* **目标**：预测保留的测试集的质量分数（发布时不包含标签或参考图像）。最终排名基于该阶段。在两个阶段中，预测都是直接在失真图像上进行的，提交结果可以是**连续分数**——不需要整数评分。

---

## 评估

提交结果根据预测质量分数与基准真值之间的相关性进行评估：

* **皮尔逊线性相关系数（PLCC）**：衡量预测分数与基准真值之间的线性关系。
* **斯皮尔曼秩序相关系数（SRCC）**：衡量预测分数与基准真值之间的单调关系（排名一致性）。

最终排名分数是**PLCC和SRCC的平均值**，这是排行榜上显示的唯一列。

---

## 联系方式

如有任何疑问，请联系：

* **邮箱**：lcysyzxdxc@sjtu.edu.cn

The file must follow the specific formatting and column requirements. **File Structure:** * **Archive**: `submission.zip` * **Content**: `submission.tsv` **TSV Header Requirements:** The TSV file must include the following two columns: 1. **index**: The unique identifier for each distorted image (the image filename, including the `.png` extension). 2. **quality**: Your predicted quality score for each image (floating-point value). **Note:** Predictions may be any **continuous values** — integer ratings are not required. **Example TSV Content:**

AIGI_DALLE3_003_T01_S4.png 3.1246
AIGI_DALLE3_003_T02_S4.png 2.0327
AIGI_DALLE3_003_T03_S5.png 2.9875
... ...
> **Test Phase Submission Format Example** > > Download the **Test Submission Template** to see a working example of the **test phase** submission structure. **(待发布 / Coming soon)** --- ## 2. Evaluation Metrics Submissions are evaluated based on their correlation with the Ground Truth (GT) scores. We use two primary statistical metrics to assess the accuracy of your predictions: * **Pearson Linear Correlation Coefficient (PLCC)**: Measures the linear relationship between the predicted scores and the ground truth. * **Spearman Rank-Order Correlation Coefficient (SRCC)**: Measures the monotonic relationship (ranking consistency) between the predicted scores and the ground truth. --- ## 3. Leaderboard Ranking The competition features a single ranking track. * **Quality Score (PLCC & SRCC Mean)** * Evaluated as the mean of PLCC and SRCC computed between the predicted quality scores and the ground truth. This is the only column shown on the leaderboard. --- ## 4. Important Notes * **Consistency**: Ensure the `index` column matches the Test Set exactly. Any missing rows or mismatched indices will result in a submission error. * **Encoding**: Do not include image data in your submission; only the predicted scores are required. * **Precision**: We recommend providing scores with at least 4 decimal places for better ranking granularity.

pages.title: Overview
pages.content: # Welcome to Track 2: HA-VLN **Human-Aware Vision-and-Language Navigation (HA-VLN)** is Track 2 of [RoboWorld 2026](https://roboworld2026.github.io/), affiliated with the [RoboPAD Workshop at NeurIPS 2026](https://robotpad2026.github.io/). ## Challenge Overview This track challenges participants to develop **human-aware vision-and-language navigation agents** that follow natural-language instructions **safely, efficiently, and socially** in dynamic human environments. While many standard VLN benchmarks assume static scenes, real-world spaces are shared with moving people who serve as both semantic landmarks and dynamic obstacles. Built on [HA-VLN 2.0](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14229), submissions must balance **instruction following** and **social compliance** under partial observability and real-time human interactions. - **Human-Referenced Grounding**: Interpret fine-grained instructions that reference both scene landmarks and ongoing human activities. - **Social Norm Compliance**: Respect personal space, proactively avoid human collisions, and navigate safely around moving bystanders. - **Realistic Benchmarking**: Navigate indoor and outdoor areas with multi-human interactions in the HA-R2R and HAPS 2.0 datasets. We welcome navigation policies, waypoint and topological planners, world models, and VLA approaches that advance safe, human-centered navigation in shared spaces. ## Task Definition - **Input:** A natural-language instruction and sequential egocentric RGB-D observations. - **Setting:** **Closed-loop interactive navigation** in continuous 3D environments with dynamic humans. - **Actions:** Six discrete actions: `STOP`, `MOVE_FORWARD`, `TURN_LEFT`, `TURN_RIGHT`, `LOOK_UP`, `LOOK_DOWN`. - **Output:** An ordered sequence of actions (1 to 500 steps, ending in `STOP`) submitted for official simulator replay. - **Objective:** Reach the instructed goal safely while avoiding collisions with humans. ## Phases - Phase 1: Development on released val_seen and val_unseen episodes. Both splits are reported; only the val_unseen Score determines the Phase 1 ranking. - Phase 1 coverage: submit actions for all 778 val_seen episodes and all 1,839 val_unseen episodes. - Phase 2: Final evaluation on withheld test scoring data. The test Score determines final rankings and awards. Phase 1 scores do not determine shortlisting or awards and are not combined with Phase 2 scores. Submit at most five times per day and 100 times per phase; the best Score is retained. ## Schedule 1. Registration opens October 08, 2026. 2. Phase 1 opens October 15, 2026, and closes October 30, 2026. 3. Phase 2 opens October 30, 2026, and closes November 30, 2026. 4. Award decisions are announced on December 12, 2026. ## Awards & Recognition 1. **Certificates of Recognition**: Official certificates awarded to the Top 5 teams in Track 2. 2. **Best Innovative Solution**: Certificate recognizing outstanding creativity and technical innovation. 3. **Oral Presentations**: Selected top-performing teams will be invited to give oral presentations at the RoboPAD Workshop at NeurIPS 2026. Final rankings and awards are determined entirely by Phase 2 test evaluation. ## Materials & Toolkit - [Challenge repository and participant toolkit](https://github.com/roboworld2026/track2): Documentation, data download scripts, baseline setup, and action submission exporter. - [Track website](https://roboworld2026.github.io/track2): Official track details and announcements. - [HA-VLN 2.0](https://uwmilab.github.io/HA-VLN-webpage/): Project page and [official repository](https://github.com/UWMILab/HA-VLN). - Starting kit: Download the Phase 1 starting kit attached to this competition for the official episode manifest, example submission, and local validator. ## Registration Register your team through the [Google Form](https://roboworld2026.github.io/#registration) (registration opens October 08, 2026) to be eligible for the leaderboard, certificates, and awards. ## Contact - **Technical Support:** [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/roboworld2026/track2/issues) - **Event & Registration:** [roboworld2026@gmail.com](mailto:roboworld2026@gmail.com) - **Discord:** [Join the RoboWorld Track 2 Discord](https://discord.gg/S8s8JcxtT) - **WeChat Group:** [Join the RoboWorld Track 2 WeChat Group](https://github.com/roboworld2026/roboworld2026.github.io/blob/main/wechat_track2.JPG)

欢迎来到赛道2：HA-VLN

**具人感知视觉语言导航（HA-VLN）**是 [RoboWorld 2026](https://roboworld2026.github.io/) 的赛道2，隶属于 [NeurIPS 2026 RoboPAD研讨会](https://robotpad2026.github.io/)。

## 挑战赛概述

本赛道要求参赛者开发**具人感知视觉语言导航智能体**，使其能够在动态人体环境中**安全、高效且符合社交规范**地遵循自然语言指令。

尽管许多标准VLN基准测试假设场景是静态的，但真实世界空间与移动的人群共享，这些人既是语义地标也是动态障碍物。基于 [HA-VLN 2.0](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14229)，提交作品必须在部分可观测性和实时人体交互的条件下，平衡**指令遵循**与**社交合规性**。

- **人参考接地**：解读同时参考场景地标和正在进行的人体活动的细粒度指令。
- **社会规范遵守**：尊重个人空间，主动避免与人体碰撞，并安全地绕行移动旁观者。
- **真实基准测试**：在HA-R2R和HAPS 2.0数据集中，在具有多人体交互的室内和室外区域进行导航。

我们欢迎导航策略、路点和拓扑规划器、世界模型以及VLA（视觉语言动作）方法，以推动共享空间中安全、以人为中心的导航技术发展。

## 任务定义

- **输入**：自然语言指令和连续的以自我为中心的RGB-D观测。
- **设置**：在具有动态人体的连续3D环境中进行**闭环交互式导航**。
- **动作**：六个离散动作：`停止`、`前进`、`左转`、`右转`、`抬头`、`低头`。
- **输出**：动作的有序序列（1到500步，以`停止`结束），提交至官方模拟器回放。
- **目标**：安全到达指令目标，同时避免与人体碰撞。

## 阶段

- 第一阶段：在已发布的验证集已见（val_seen）和验证集未见（val_unseen）片段上进行开发。两个划分都会被报告；仅验证集未见的分数决定第一阶段排名。
- 第一阶段覆盖范围：为全部778个验证集已见片段和全部1,839个验证集未见片段提交动作。
- 第二阶段：在保留的测试评分数据上进行最终评估。测试分数决定最终排名和奖项。

第一阶段分数不决定入围或奖项，也不与第二阶段分数合并。每天最多提交5次，每阶段最多提交100次；保留最佳分数。

## 日程安排

1. 报名开始：2026年10月08日。
2. 第一阶段开放：2026年10月15日，截止：2026年10月30日。
3. 第二阶段开放：2026年10月30日，截止：2026年11月30日。
4. 奖项决定公布：2026年12月12日。

## 奖项与认可

1. **认可证书**：颁发给赛道2前5名团队的官方证书。
2. **最佳创新解决方案**：表彰杰出创意和技术创新的证书。
3. **口头报告**：精选的顶尖表现团队将被邀请在NeurIPS 2026 RoboPAD研讨会上进行口头报告。

最终排名和奖项完全由第二阶段测试评估决定。

- [挑战赛代码库和参赛工具包](https://github.com/roboworld2026/track2)：文档、数据下载脚本、基线设置和动作提交导出器。

- 入门套件：下载附加于本次竞赛的第一阶段入门套件，获取官方片段清单、示例提交和本地验证器。

## 报名

通过 [Google表单](https://roboworld2026.github.io/#registration)
（报名开放时间为2026年10月08日）注册您的团队，以获得排行榜、证书和参赛资格。

pages.title: Submission & Evaluation
pages.content:
# Submission & Evaluation

Both phases accept a single ZIP archive containing predicted action sequences for all required episodes.

## What the Submission Contains

Submit one ZIP archive containing action sequences for every episode in the phase manifest. Only action predictions are used for evaluation; model weights, code, and external environment assets are not required.

## Archive Layout

Place the prediction JSON files directly at the root of the ZIP archive:

```text
submission.zip
|-- val_seen.json      # 778 episodes
`-- val_unseen.json    # 1,839 episodes
```

Phase 2 follows the same layout with `test.json` in `submission_test.zip`. Package Phase 1 predictions:

```bash
zip -j submission.zip val_seen.json val_unseen.json
```

## Prediction File Structure

Each JSON file must contain `format_version`, `split`, and `episodes`:

```json
{
  "format_version": 1,
  "split": "val_unseen",
  "episodes": [
    {
      "episode_id": "synthetic-example-001",
      "actions": ["MOVE_FORWARD", "TURN_LEFT", "LOOK_UP", "LOOK_DOWN", "STOP"]
    }
  ]
}
```

- `format_version`: Set to `1`.
- `split`: `"val_seen"`, `"val_unseen"`, or `"test"`, matching the corresponding phase.
- `episodes`: A list of episode predictions covering all episode IDs in the manifest.
  - `episode_id`: String identifier matching the manifest exactly once.
  - `actions`: An ordered list of 1 to 500 actions chosen from `["STOP", "MOVE_FORWARD", "TURN_LEFT", "TURN_RIGHT", "LOOK_UP", "LOOK_DOWN"]`. `"STOP"` may only appear as the final action; sequences shorter than 500 actions must end with `"STOP"`.

## Evaluation & Leaderboard

Submissions are evaluated on navigation and social compliance, and ranked by the composite challenge **Score** (higher is better):

- **SR** (higher is better): Collision-free navigation success rate to the target goal.
- **NE** (lower is better): Mean Euclidean distance in metres from final agent position to goal.
- **CR** (lower is better): Ratio of collision episodes over human-influenced episodes.
- **TCR** (lower is better): Mean number of collision events per episode.

```text
NE utility  = 3 / (3 + NE)
TCR utility = 1 / (1 + TCR)
Navigation  = 0.80 * SR + 0.20 * NE utility
Social      = 0.75 * (1 - CR) + 0.25 * TCR utility
Score       = 100 * Navigation * (0.70 + 0.30 * Social)
```

Phase 1 ranks teams by `val_unseen` Score (`val_seen` is reported for reference). Phase 2 ranks teams by `test` Score to determine final awards. When Scores are tied, rankings are broken in order: higher SR, lower NE, lower CR, lower TCR, and earlier submission time.

## Submission Limits

Each team may submit up to 5 times per day and 100 times per phase. The leaderboard retains the team's highest Score.

## Support

- **Technical Support:** [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/roboworld2026/track2/issues)  
- **Event & Registration:** [roboworld2026@gmail.com](mailto:roboworld2026@gmail.com)

## 评估与排行榜

提交结果根据导航和社交合规性进行评估，并按综合挑战**分数**进行排名（越高越好）：

- **SR**（越高越好）：到达目标的无碰撞导航成功率。
- **NE**（越低越好）：智能体最终位置到目标的平均欧几里得距离（米）。
- **CR**（越低越好）：碰撞回合与受人类影响回合的比率。
- **TCR**（越低越好）：每回合的平均碰撞事件次数。

```text
NE utility  = 3 / (3 + NE)
TCR utility = 1 / (1 + TCR)
Navigation  = 0.80 * SR + 0.20 * NE utility
Social      = 0.75 * (1 - CR) + 0.25 * TCR utility
Score       = 100 * Navigation * (0.70 + 0.30 * Social)
```

第一阶段根据`val_unseen`分数对队伍进行排名（`val_seen`分数仅供参考）。第二阶段根据`test`分数对队伍进行排名以确定最终奖项。当分数相同时，按以下顺序打破平局：更高的SR、更低的NE、更低的CR、更低的TCR、更早的提交时间。

## 提交限制

每支队伍每天最多可提交5次，每个阶段最多可提交100次。排行榜保留队伍的最高分数。

pages.content:
UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge — V2X-Real Track

Update — Due to increased interest from multiple qualified participants, Letters of Intent are now accepted through October 30, 2026, 8:00 PM EDT, aligned with the close of the development phase. Teams that have already submitted an LOI by email need take no further action. Teams joining now can register via our Letter of Intent Form.

Update — the Letter of Intent deadline is extended to August 15, 2026 (previously July 25). All other dates are unchanged.

A track of the 2026 IEEE Big Data Cup, held in conjunction with the IEEE International Conference on Big Data (IEEE BigData) 2026, Phoenix, AZ, USA.

Roadside LiDAR perception for intelligent transportation systems is bottlenecked by the cost and rarity of large, well-annotated real datasets. This challenge asks: can synthetic LiDAR data be made realistic enough that a deep learning model trained on it generalizes to real LiDAR frames?

Towards that, this challenge asks participants to generate their own synthetic LiDAR data targeting the V2X-Real distribution, train an object detector on that data, and submit detections on real held-out frames. We score on (1) how distributionally close their synthetic frames are to real ones, and (2) how well the sim-only detector performs on real frames.

Important Dates

  • Letter of Intent Deadline: August 15, 2026 (extended from July 25)
  • Final Report and Solution Submission Deadline: November 15, 2026
  • Winning Teams Announcement: November 25, 2026
  • Conference: December 14–17, 2026

Reference resources for participants

To support participants who would like a documented starting point, we make publicly available a complete reference pipeline covering synthesis methodology, empirical analysis, ready-to-use synthetic datasets, and an open-source LiDAR data processing and visualization software. These materials are offered as orientation, not as requirements.

The synthesis pipeline is described in UrbanTwin: Building High-Fidelity Digital Twins for Sim2Real LiDAR Perception and Evaluation (arXiv preprint), with a deeper empirical analysis including the distributional realism metrics adopted by this challenge in High-Fidelity Digital Twins for Bridging the Sim2Real Gap in LiDAR-Based ITS Perception (IEEE T-ITS, 2026).

The synthetic LiDAR datasets generated with that pipeline are released in UrbanTwin: Synthetic Roadside LiDAR Datasets (IEEE OJ-ITS, 2026) and are available for download at Harvard Dataverse. Each dataset contains 10K frames annotated across six object categories for detection, tracking, and segmentation tasks, and is directly compatible with the multi-class evaluation used here; empirical analysis in papers include both the distributional realism metrics and single-class 3D object detection study as proof-of-concept. For end-to-end LiDAR processing we also provide our LiGuard Framework (IEEE T-IV, 2026) with short, more software focused read on The Journal of Open Source Software.

What you will do

  1. Download the public real V2X-Real dataset and the released detection-test point clouds (50 real frames, no labels).
  2. Generate synthetic LiDAR frames using any approach you like — simulation (CARLA, LGSVL, custom), generative models (diffusion, GANs, flow-based), hybrid pipelines, or anything else.
  3. Train a 3D object detector (any architecture) on only your synthetic data.
  4. Submit:
    • 50 of your synthetic LiDAR frames,
    • your detector's predictions on the 50 released test point clouds,
    • and a signed honor declaration.

Scoring at a glance

Combined score = 0.6 × normalized 3D mAP + 0.4 × normalized realism, where 3D mAP is averaged across the 3 object categories defined for this track (vehicle, pedestrian, truck) and realism averages normalized Chamfer Distance, MMD, EMD, and Fréchet Point-cloud Distance. See the Evaluation tab for the formulae.

Prizes

Per track:

  • 1st place: USD 500
  • 2nd place: USD 300
  • 3rd place: USD 200

Sponsor(s) will be announced before the Development phase opens.

Phases

  • Development — public leaderboard, up to 5 submissions/day per participant, 100 total. Use this to iterate.
  • Final — private leaderboard until close, 5 total submissions per participant. The final-phase ranking determines the winners.

Baselines

Reference numbers are listed in the Data tab.

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
Evaluation Protocol

Two scores are computed and combined into a single Combined score that determines leaderboard rank.

1. Distributional realism

Aggregation:

  1. Concatenate the 50 submitted synthetic frames into one set S_syn; concatenate the 50 held-out real reference frames into S_real.
  2. Mask both to the point-cloud range [-40, -40, -8, 40, 40, 2].
  3. Subsample uniformly at random to N = 10,000 points per side, with seed 1234 (identical seed used by the local evaluator in the starter kit).
  4. Compute one CD, MMD, EMD, and FPD across the entire 10,000-point sets.

1a. Chamfer Distance (CD)

CD(P, Q) = (1/|P|) Σ_{p ∈ P} min_{q ∈ Q} ||p - q||²
         + (1/|Q|) Σ_{q ∈ Q} min_{p ∈ P} ||p - q||²

Squared-L2 nearest-neighbor cost; symmetric. Lower is better.

1b. Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD)

MMD²(X, Y) = E[k(x, x')] + E[k(y, y')] - 2 E[k(x, y)],   k(a, b) = exp(-γ ||a - b||²)

Unbiased estimator (off-diagonal). Bandwidth γ is set by the median heuristic on a 1 000-point joint subsample (γ = 1 / (2 · median ||x - y||²)) so the kernel does not saturate at LiDAR spatial scales. Lower is better.

1c. Earth Mover's Distance (EMD)

EMD(X, Y) = √ ( min_{T ∈ Π(X, Y)} Σ_{i,j} T_{ij} · ||x_i - y_j|| )

Wasserstein-1 with Euclidean ground cost, solved exactly by the network simplex (POT's ot.emd2). Reported in metres. Lower is better.

1d. Fréchet Point-cloud Distance (FPD)

FPD = ||μ_X - μ_Y||² + Tr(Σ_X + Σ_Y - 2 (Σ_X · Σ_Y)^{1/2})

FID-style: fits a 3-variate Gaussian to each set's points, computes the 2-Wasserstein between Gaussians. Lower is better.

2. 3D Object Detection

Participants submit detections (predictions.json) on 50 real LiDAR frames whose ground truth is held out. We compute average precision over the 3 object categories defined for this track (vehicle, pedestrian, truck), at IoU thresholds 0.5 (primary) and 0.7 (secondary). Per-class AP is reported, and mean AP across classes (mAP) is the leaderboard's detection score; classes with zero ground-truth instances in the held-out set are excluded from the mean. Both KITTI 11-point and 40-point interpolated AP are reported; the 40-point form is the leaderboard primary.

Ground-truth and predicted boxes use the OpenPCDet 7-DoF format [x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, heading]. IoU is computed as 3D intersection-over-union between two oriented BEV rectangles times the Z overlap. The KITTI truncation/occlusion/min-height difficulty filter is not applied because those depend on 2D bounding-box annotations that are not natural for roadside LiDAR datasets.

The valid class strings for this track are listed in config.json (shipped in reference_data/) and in submission_format.md in the starter kit. Any prediction with an unrecognized class label is discarded.

3. Combined score

Each component is min-max normalized into [0, 1] using a per-track normalization range:

score_realism   = mean( norm(CD), norm(MMD), norm(EMD), norm(FPD) )    (lower-is-better → 1 - clip)
score_detection = norm( AP_3d @ IoU 0.5 )                               (higher-is-better → clip)
score_combined  = 0.6 · score_detection + 0.4 · score_realism

Normalization endpoints are public in config.json (shipped in reference_data/), so the local evaluator and the server compute identical scores.

Reproducibility

  • Realism is dataset-level — frame ordering does not matter. Submit the 50 synthetic frames in any consistent naming.
  • Subsampling RNG seed: 1234 (same on server and starting kit).
  • The exact scoring program shipped to the Codabench worker is included in the starting kit.
pages.content_zh:
评估协议

计算两个分数并合并为一个综合分数，以确定排行榜排名。

1. 分布真实性

聚合：

  1. 将50个提交的合成帧拼接为一个集合S_syn；将50个保留的真实参考帧拼接为S_real。
  2. 将两者掩码限制在点云范围[-40, -40, -8, 40, 40, 2]内。
  3. 使用随机种子1234（与入门套件中本地评估器使用的种子相同）对每侧均匀随机子采样至N = 10,000点。
  4. 在整个10,000点集上计算一次CD、MMD、EMD和FPD。

1a. 倒角距离（CD）

CD(P, Q) = (1/|P|) Σ_{p ∈ P} min_{q ∈ Q} ||p - q||²
         + (1/|Q|) Σ_{q ∈ Q} min_{p ∈ P} ||p - q||²

平方L2最近邻代价；对称。越低越好。

1b. 最大均值差异（MMD）

MMD²(X, Y) = E[k(x, x')] + E[k(y, y')] - 2 E[k(x, y)],   k(a, b) = exp(-γ ||a - b||²)

无偏估计量（非对角）。带宽γ通过1,000点联合子样本的中位数启发式设置（γ = 1 / (2 · 中位数 ||x - y||²)），以确保核函数在LiDAR空间尺度上不饱和。越低越好。

1c. 推土机距离（EMD）

EMD(X, Y) = √ ( min_{T ∈ Π(X, Y)} Σ_{i,j} T_{ij} · ||x_i - y_j|| )

使用欧几里得地面成本的Wasserstein-1距离，通过网络单纯形法（POT的ot.emd2）精确求解。以米为单位报告。越低越好。

1d. Fréchet点云距离（FPD）

FPD = ||μ_X - μ_Y||² + Tr(Σ_X + Σ_Y - 2 (Σ_X · Σ_Y)^{1/2})

类FID风格：对每个集合的点拟合三元高斯分布，计算高斯分布之间的2-Wasserstein距离。越低越好。

2. 3D目标检测

参与者对50个真实LiDAR帧提交检测结果（predictions.json），这些帧的真实标签被保留。我们在该赛道定义的3个目标类别（车辆、行人、卡车）上计算平均精度，IoU阈值分别为0.5（主要）和0.7（次要）。报告每类AP，跨类别的平均AP（mAP）作为排行榜的检测分数；在保留集中没有真实实例的类别不参与平均计算。报告KITTI 11点和40点插值AP两种形式；40点形式是排行榜的主要指标。

真实标签和预测框使用OpenPCDet 7自由度格式[x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, heading]。IoU计算为两个定向BEV矩形之间的3D交并比乘以Z轴重叠率。不应用KITTI的截断/遮挡/最小高度难度过滤，因为这些依赖于2D边界框标注，而这对于路边LiDAR数据集并不自然。

该赛道的有效类别字符串列于config.json（位于reference_data/中）和入门套件的submission_format.md中。任何带有无法识别类别标签的预测将被丢弃。

3. 综合分数

每个分量使用按赛道归一化范围进行最小-最大归一化至[0, 1]：

score_realism   = 均值( norm(CD), norm(MMD), norm(EMD), norm(FPD) )    （越低越好 → 1 - 裁剪）
score_detection = norm( AP_3d @ IoU 0.5 )                               （越高越好 → 裁剪）
score_combined  = 0.6 · score_detection + 0.4 · score_realism

归一化端点在config.json中公开（位于reference_data/中），因此本地评估器和服务器计算出的分数相同。

Data

V2X-Real

Real V2X-Real data is publicly available from its original release. We do not redistribute it. Participants must obtain the real dataset directly from its source under its own license.

  • Source: https://github.com/ucla-mobility/V2X-Real
  • License: see the source.

Released for participants

The starting kit (Files tab → starting_kit) contains:

  • detection_test_frames/ — 50 real LiDAR frames (point clouds only, no labels) on which you must run your detector and submit predictions.
  • detection_test_frame_ids.json — the canonical list of frame IDs your predictions.json must cover, in order.
  • forbidden_frames.txt — 100 frame IDs you may not train, validate, or hyperparameter-tune on. This is the union of the 50 detection-test frames and the 50 realism-reference frames. Honor system, enforced by signed declaration in your submission.
  • local_eval.py — the exact scoring program shipped to the Codabench worker. Run it locally to reproduce server scores bit-for-bit, given a dummy reference set you generate from the released detection-test frames.
  • make_dummy_submission.py — produces a known-bad submission that exercises the format. Useful for sanity-checking your pipeline.
  • submission_format.md — full submission spec.

Held out (organizer-only)

  • 50 real frames used as the realism reference set.
  • Ground-truth boxes for the 50 detection-test frames.

Categories evaluated

This track is scored on 3 object categories defined for the V2X-Real dataset: vehicle, pedestrian, truck. The leaderboard's detection score is the mean AP across these categories; classes with zero ground-truth instances in the held-out 50-frame set are excluded from the mean.

Splits

Splits are stratified random samples with fixed seed 1234. The exact frame ID lists are published in the starting kit so anyone can reproduce them from the released real dataset.

Reference baselines

The leaderboard's detection score is the mean AP across all categories defined for this track (see Evaluation), so submissions are scored on broader coverage than these single-class references. pages.title: Submission
pages.content:
Submission Format

Pack everything below into a single submission.zip and upload it on the Submit tab.

submission.zip
├── synthetic/
│   ├── 0001.bin
│   ├── 0002.bin
│   ├── ...
│   └── 0050.bin           # exactly 50 files
├── predictions.json
└── declaration.pdf        # signed honor declaration (PDF). declaration.txt also accepted.

synthetic/<id>.bin

  • Exactly 50 files.
  • Each file is raw float32, shape N × 3, in row-major order, with channels (x, y, z) in metres.
  • Either N × 3 or N × 4 (xyz + intensity) is accepted; the intensity column, if present, is dropped before scoring.
  • Each file ≤ 1.5 MB on disk (~125,000 points). Realism is computed at the dataset level: all 50 frames are concatenated, masked to the track's point-cloud range, then subsampled to 10,000 points (seed 1234) before computing CD / MMD / EMD / FPD. Submitting denser frames does not improve scores; frame ordering does not matter.
  • The simplest valid naming is 0001.bin … 0050.bin.

predictions.json

JSON object whose keys are the frame IDs from detection_test_frame_ids.json (in the starting kit). For every frame ID you must include an entry, even if the value is an empty list.

{
  "<frame_id_1>": [
    {"box": [x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, heading], "score": 0.97, "class": "vehicle"},
    {"box": [...],                          "score": 0.81, "class": "pedestrian"}
  ],
  "<frame_id_2>": [],
  ...
}
  • box: 7 floats, OpenPCDet convention. (x, y, z) is the box center in metres in the LiDAR frame, (dx, dy, dz) are full extents along the box-local axes, heading is rotation around +Z in radians.
  • score: confidence in [0, 1].
  • class: one of the valid class strings for this track. Valid values: vehicle, pedestrian, truck. Class strings are matched case-insensitively. Predictions with unrecognized class strings are discarded before AP is computed.

declaration.pdf (or declaration.txt)

The starter kit ships declaration_template.pdf, a one-page form with the required honor statement preprinted and a signature line. Fill in team name and date, sign (digitally with any PDF tool, or print → sign → scan), save as declaration.pdf, and include it in every submission.

If you cannot easily produce a signed PDF, a plain declaration.txt is also accepted. Required statement (verbatim, case-insensitive):

I confirm that I did not train on any frame listed in forbidden_frames.txt, and that all submitted detections were produced by a model trained only on synthetic data I generated.

What gets returned

After scoring (typically < 5 minutes for valid submissions) you'll see your position on the leaderboard plus a Detailed Results view with all component metrics, including per-class AP.

提交格式

将以下内容全部打包到单个 submission.zip 文件中，并在提交标签页上传。

submission.zip
├── synthetic/
│   ├── 0001.bin
│   ├── 0002.bin
│   ├── ...
│   └── 0050.bin           # 恰好 50 个文件

synthetic/<id>.bin

predictions.json

JSON 对象，其键为 detection_test_frame_ids.json（在初始工具包中）中的帧 ID。对于每个帧 ID，都必须包含一个条目，即使值为空列表。

{
  "<frame_id_1>": [
    {"box": [x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, heading], "score": 0.97, "class": "vehicle"},
    {"box": [...],                          "score": 0.81, "class": "pedestrian"}
  ],
  "<frame_id_2>": [],
  ...
}
  • box：7 个浮点数，遵循 OpenPCDet 约定。(x, y, z) 为框中心在激光雷达坐标系中的位置（单位：米），(dx, dy, dz) 为沿框局部轴的全尺寸，heading 为绕 +Z 轴的旋转（弧度）。

  • class：该赛道的有效类别字符串之一。有效值：vehicle、pedestrian、truck。类别字符串不区分大小写匹配。包含无法识别类别字符串的预测在计算 AP 前会被丢弃。
