如果您无法轻松生成带签名的 PDF，也接受纯文本 declaration.txt。所需声明（原文，不区分大小写）：

我确认我未使用 forbidden_frames.txt 中列出的任何帧进行训练，且所有提交的检测结果均由仅基于我生成的合成数据训练的模型产生。

返回内容

评分后（有效提交通常少于 5 分钟），您将在排行榜上看到自己的位置，以及包含所有组件指标（包括每类 AP）的详细结果视图。

Rules

Eligibility

  • Open to anyone — researchers, students, industry teams.
  • Each team must register one participant account; do not maintain multiple accounts.

Allowed

  • Any simulation framework or generative model (CARLA, Helios++, OpenScene, neural radiance fields, diffusion, GANs, custom physics). Open or closed source — what matters is the synthesized data.
  • Any 3D object detector architecture, trained on your synthetic data only.
  • Augmentations applied during detector training (rotation, scale, flip, ground-truth sampling, noise) — they operate on synthetic data, not on the forbidden real frames.
  • Using the train split of the public real dataset for hyperparameter selection or domain adaptation, provided no forbidden frame is touched. (The forbidden list contains only the 100 reserved frames, not the entire real train split.)

Forbidden

  • Training, validating, hyperparameter-tuning, or otherwise observing ground truth from any of the 100 frames listed in forbidden_frames.txt. This is enforced by signed declaration and is the foundational integrity rule of the challenge.
  • Submitting predictions produced by a model that has been trained on real labels for any roadside-LiDAR dataset. The detector must be sim-only.
  • Reverse-engineering or inferring the held-out realism reference frames via Codabench's leaderboard signal (e.g., probing submissions designed to leak the reference set's identity). Submissions found to be doing this will be disqualified.
  • Multiple accounts, sub-team accounts, or coordinating across registered teams.

Disqualification

Organizers reserve the right to inspect the synthetic frames and predictions of any submission for evidence of forbidden-frame leakage (e.g., synthetic frames that suspiciously resemble held-out real frames; predictions whose distribution implies access to held-out ground truth). Disqualified participants are removed from the leaderboard and from prize consideration.

Prizes

Per track: 1st place USD 500, 2nd place USD 300, 3rd place USD 200. Sponsor(s) will be announced before the Development phase opens.

Publication and credit

  • Every participating team submits a 4–8 page challenge report describing their approach, due by the final-phase deadline (November 15, 2026).
  • Teams that prefer not to publish may opt into the non-publication track for their submission.
  • Top-3 teams per track are invited to present at the IEEE BigData 2026 Big Data Cup workshop session in Phoenix, AZ (December 14–17, 2026), and to submit a full paper to the IEEE BigData 2026 proceedings through the challenge's associated paper track.
  • The challenge organizers may publish an aggregate analysis of all submissions (anonymized unless explicit permission is granted).

pages.content:
UrbanTwin Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge — LUMPI Track

Update — Due to increased interest from multiple qualified participants, Letters of Intent are now accepted through October 30, 2026, 8:00 PM EDT, aligned with the close of the development phase. Teams that have already submitted an LOI by email need take no further action. Teams joining now can register via our Letter of Intent Form.

Update — the Letter of Intent deadline is extended to August 15, 2026 (previously July 25). All other dates are unchanged.

A track of the 2026 IEEE Big Data Cup, held in conjunction with the IEEE International Conference on Big Data (IEEE BigData) 2026, Phoenix, AZ, USA.

Roadside LiDAR perception for intelligent transportation systems is bottlenecked by the cost and rarity of large, well-annotated real datasets. This challenge asks: can synthetic LiDAR data be made realistic enough that a deep learning model trained on it generalizes to real LiDAR frames?

Towards that, this challenge asks participants to generate their own synthetic LiDAR data targeting the LUMPI distribution, train an object detector on that data, and submit detections on real held-out frames. We score on (1) how distributionally close their synthetic frames are to real ones, and (2) how well the sim-only detector performs on real frames.

Important Dates

  • Letter of Intent Deadline: August 15, 2026 (extended from July 25)
  • Final Report and Solution Submission Deadline: November 15, 2026
  • Winning Teams Announcement: November 25, 2026
  • Conference: December 14–17, 2026

Reference resources for participants

To support participants who would like a documented starting point, we make publicly available a complete reference pipeline covering synthesis methodology, empirical analysis, ready-to-use synthetic datasets, and an open-source LiDAR data processing and visualization software. These materials are offered as orientation, not as requirements.

The synthesis pipeline is described in UrbanTwin: Building High-Fidelity Digital Twins for Sim2Real LiDAR Perception and Evaluation (arXiv preprint), with a deeper empirical analysis including the distributional realism metrics adopted by this challenge in High-Fidelity Digital Twins for Bridging the Sim2Real Gap in LiDAR-Based ITS Perception (IEEE T-ITS, 2026).

The synthetic LiDAR datasets generated with that pipeline are released in UrbanTwin: Synthetic Roadside LiDAR Datasets (IEEE OJ-ITS, 2026) and are available for download at Harvard Dataverse. Each dataset contains 10K frames annotated across six object categories for detection, tracking, and segmentation tasks, and is directly compatible with the multi-class evaluation used here; empirical analysis in papers include both the distributional realism metrics and single-class 3D object detection study as proof-of-concept. For end-to-end LiDAR processing we also provide our LiGuard Framework (IEEE T-IV, 2026) with short, more software focused read on The Journal of Open Source Software.

What you will do

  1. Download the public real LUMPI dataset and the released detection-test point clouds (50 real frames, no labels).
  2. Generate synthetic LiDAR frames using any approach you like — simulation (CARLA, LGSVL, custom), generative models (diffusion, GANs, flow-based), hybrid pipelines, or anything else.
  3. Train a 3D object detector (any architecture) on only your synthetic data.
  4. Submit:
    • 50 of your synthetic LiDAR frames,
    • your detector's predictions on the 50 released test point clouds,
    • and a signed honor declaration.

Scoring at a glance

Combined score = 0.6 × normalized 3D mAP + 0.4 × normalized realism, where 3D mAP is averaged across the 8 object categories defined for this track (Person, Car, Bicycle, Motorcycle, Bus, Truck, Van, Unknown) and realism averages normalized Chamfer Distance, MMD, EMD, and Fréchet Point-cloud Distance. See the Evaluation tab for the formulae.

Prizes

Per track:

  • 1st place: USD 500
  • 2nd place: USD 300
  • 3rd place: USD 200

Sponsor(s) will be announced before the Development phase opens.

Phases

  • Development — public leaderboard, up to 5 submissions/day per participant, 100 total. Use this to iterate.
  • Final — private leaderboard until close, 5 total submissions per participant. The final-phase ranking determines the winners.

Baselines

Reference numbers are listed in the Data tab.

pages.title: Evaluation
pages.content:
Evaluation Protocol

Two scores are computed and combined into a single Combined score that determines leaderboard rank.

1. Distributional realism

Aggregation:

  1. Concatenate the 50 submitted synthetic frames into one set S_syn; concatenate the 50 held-out real reference frames into S_real.
  2. Mask both to the point-cloud range [-40, -40, -5, 40, 40, 5].
  3. Subsample uniformly at random to N = 10,000 points per side, with seed 1234 (identical seed used by the local evaluator in the starter kit).
  4. Compute one CD, MMD, EMD, and FPD across the entire 10,000-point sets.

1a. Chamfer Distance (CD)

CD(P, Q) = (1/|P|) Σ_{p ∈ P} min_{q ∈ Q} ||p - q||²
         + (1/|Q|) Σ_{q ∈ Q} min_{p ∈ P} ||p - q||²

Squared-L2 nearest-neighbor cost; symmetric. Lower is better.

1b. Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD)

MMD²(X, Y) = E[k(x, x')] + E[k(y, y')] - 2 E[k(x, y)],   k(a, b) = exp(-γ ||a - b||²)

Unbiased estimator (off-diagonal). Bandwidth γ is set by the median heuristic on a 1 000-point joint subsample (γ = 1 / (2 · median ||x - y||²)) so the kernel does not saturate at LiDAR spatial scales. Lower is better.

1c. Earth Mover's Distance (EMD)

EMD(X, Y) = √ ( min_{T ∈ Π(X, Y)} Σ_{i,j} T_{ij} · ||x_i - y_j|| )

Wasserstein-1 with Euclidean ground cost, solved exactly by the network simplex (POT's ot.emd2). Reported in metres. Lower is better.

1d. Fréchet Point-cloud Distance (FPD)

FPD = ||μ_X - μ_Y||² + Tr(Σ_X + Σ_Y - 2 (Σ_X · Σ_Y)^{1/2})

FID-style: fits a 3-variate Gaussian to each set's points, computes the 2-Wasserstein between Gaussians. Lower is better.

2. 3D Object Detection

Participants submit detections (predictions.json) on 50 real LiDAR frames whose ground truth is held out. We compute average precision over the 8 object categories defined for this track (Person, Car, Bicycle, Motorcycle, Bus, Truck, Van, Unknown), at IoU thresholds 0.5 (primary) and 0.7 (secondary). Per-class AP is reported, and mean AP across classes (mAP) is the leaderboard's detection score; classes with zero ground-truth instances in the held-out set are excluded from the mean. Both KITTI 11-point and 40-point interpolated AP are reported; the 40-point form is the leaderboard primary.

Ground-truth and predicted boxes use the OpenPCDet 7-DoF format [x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, heading]. IoU is computed as 3D intersection-over-union between two oriented BEV rectangles times the Z overlap. The KITTI truncation/occlusion/min-height difficulty filter is not applied because those depend on 2D bounding-box annotations that are not natural for roadside LiDAR datasets.

The valid class strings for this track are listed in config.json (shipped in reference_data/) and in submission_format.md in the starter kit. Any prediction with an unrecognized class label is discarded.

3. Combined score

Each component is min-max normalized into [0, 1] using a per-track normalization range:

score_realism   = mean( norm(CD), norm(MMD), norm(EMD), norm(FPD) )    (lower-is-better → 1 - clip)
score_detection = norm( AP_3d @ IoU 0.5 )                               (higher-is-better → clip)
score_combined  = 0.6 · score_detection + 0.4 · score_realism

Normalization endpoints are public in config.json (shipped in reference_data/), so the local evaluator and the server compute identical scores.

Reproducibility

  • Realism is dataset-level — frame ordering does not matter. Submit the 50 synthetic frames in any consistent naming.
  • Subsampling RNG seed: 1234 (same on server and starting kit).
  • The exact scoring program shipped to the Codabench worker is included in the starting kit.
pages.content_zh:
评估协议

计算两个得分并组合成一个综合得分，用于决定排行榜排名。

1. 分布真实性

聚合方法：

  1. 将50帧提交的合成样本拼接为集合S_syn；将50帧预留的真实参考样本拼接为S_real。
  2. 将两者掩膜至点云范围[-40, -40, -5, 40, 40, 5]。
  3. 使用随机种子1234进行均匀随机子采样，每侧保留N = 10,000个点（启动工具包中的本地评估器使用相同种子）。
  4. 在整个10,000点集合上计算一个CD、MMD、EMD和FPD。

1a. 倒角距离 (CD)

CD(P, Q) = (1/|P|) Σ_{p ∈ P} min_{q ∈ Q} ||p - q||²
         + (1/|Q|) Σ_{q ∈ Q} min_{p ∈ P} ||p - q||²

L2范数最近邻平方距离；对称。数值越低越好。

1b. 最大均值差异 (MMD)

MMD²(X, Y) = E[k(x, x')] + E[k(y, y')] - 2 E[k(x, y)],   k(a, b) = exp(-γ ||a - b||²)

无偏估计量（非对角）。带宽γ通过1,000点联合子样本的中位数启发式设置（γ = 1 / (2 · median ||x - y||²)），以确保核函数在激光雷达空间尺度下不会饱和。数值越低越好。

1c. 推土机距离 (EMD)

EMD(X, Y) = √ ( min_{T ∈ Π(X, Y)} Σ_{i,j} T_{ij} · ||x_i - y_j|| )

使用欧氏距离作为地面代价的Wasserstein-1距离，通过网络单纯形法（POT的ot.emd2）精确求解。以米为单位报告。数值越低越好。

1d. Fréchet点云距离 (FPD)

FPD = ||μ_X - μ_Y||² + Tr(Σ_X + Σ_Y - 2 (Σ_X · Σ_Y)^{1/2})

类FID方法：为每个点集拟合三维高斯分布，计算两个高斯分布之间的2-Wasserstein距离。数值越低越好。

2. 3D目标检测

参赛者提交在50帧真实激光雷达数据上的检测结果（predictions.json），其真值数据暂不公开。我们在本赛道定义的8个目标类别（行人、轿车、自行车、摩托车、公交车、卡车、货车、未知）上计算平均精度，IoU阈值分别取0.5（主要）和0.7（次要）。报告每类AP，各类别平均AP（mAP）作为排行榜的检测得分；在预留数据集中真值实例为零的类别不参与平均计算。同时报告KITTI 11点和40点插值AP；40点形式为主要排行榜依据。

真值和预测框采用OpenPCDet 7自由度格式[x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, heading]。IoU计算方式为两个定向鸟瞰图（BEV）矩形的三维交并比乘以Z轴重叠率。不应用KITTI的截断/遮挡/最小高度难度过滤，因为这些依赖于二维边界框标注，而这对路边激光雷达数据集并不自然。

本赛道的有效类别字符串列于config.json（位于reference_data/中）和启动工具包的submission_format.md中。任何类别标签无法识别的预测结果将被丢弃。

3. 综合得分

每个组成部分使用每赛道的归一化范围进行最小-最大归一化至[0, 1]区间：

score_realism   = mean( norm(CD), norm(MMD), norm(EMD), norm(FPD) )    (越低越好 → 1 - clip)
score_detection = norm( AP_3d @ IoU 0.5 )                               (越高越好 → clip)
score_combined  = 0.6 · score_detection + 0.4 · score_realism

归一化端点公开于config.json（位于reference_data/中），因此本地评估器和服务器

pages.content:
Data

LUMPI

Real LUMPI data is publicly available from its original release. We do not redistribute it. Participants must obtain the real dataset directly from its source under its own license.

  • Source: https://data.uni-hannover.de/dataset/lumpi
  • License: see the source.

Released for participants

The starting kit (Files tab → starting_kit) contains:

  • detection_test_frames/ — 50 real LiDAR frames (point clouds only, no labels) on which you must run your detector and submit predictions.
  • detection_test_frame_ids.json — the canonical list of frame IDs your predictions.json must cover, in order.
  • forbidden_frames.txt — 100 frame IDs you may not train, validate, or hyperparameter-tune on. This is the union of the 50 detection-test frames and the 50 realism-reference frames. Honor system, enforced by signed declaration in your submission.
  • local_eval.py — the exact scoring program shipped to the Codabench worker. Run it locally to reproduce server scores bit-for-bit, given a dummy reference set you generate from the released detection-test frames.
  • make_dummy_submission.py — produces a known-bad submission that exercises the format. Useful for sanity-checking your pipeline.
  • submission_format.md — full submission spec.

Held out (organizer-only)

  • 50 real frames used as the realism reference set.
  • Ground-truth boxes for the 50 detection-test frames.

Categories evaluated

This track is scored on 8 object categories defined for the LUMPI dataset: Person, Car, Bicycle, Motorcycle, Bus, Truck, Van, Unknown. The leaderboard's detection score is the mean AP across these categories; classes with zero ground-truth instances in the held-out 50-frame set are excluded from the mean.

Splits

Splits are stratified random samples with fixed seed 1234. The exact frame ID lists are published in the starting kit so anyone can reproduce them from the released real dataset.

Reference baselines

The numbers below are reported for the Car class only, taken from prior work on this dataset. The leaderboard's detection score is the mean AP across all categories defined for this track (see Evaluation), so submissions are scored on broader coverage than these single-class references. The baselines are included to demonstrate that sim → real transfer is achievable on this benchmark and to provide a per-class reference point for orientation while you iterate.

SystemCar 3D AP @ 0.5Car 3D AP @ 0.7

SEED (UT-LUMPI synthetic → real LUMPI, IEEE T-ITS 2026) 0.4474 n/r

pages.title: Submission
pages.content:
Submission Format

Pack everything below into a single submission.zip and upload it on the Submit tab.

submission.zip
├── synthetic/
│   ├── 0001.bin
│   ├── 0002.bin
│   ├── ...
│   └── 0050.bin           # exactly 50 files
├── predictions.json
└── declaration.pdf        # signed honor declaration (PDF). declaration.txt also accepted.

synthetic/<id>.bin

  • Exactly 50 files.
  • Each file is raw float32, shape N × 3, in row-major order, with channels (x, y, z) in metres.
  • Either N × 3 or N × 4 (xyz + intensity) is accepted; the intensity column, if present, is dropped before scoring.
  • Each file ≤ 1.5 MB on disk (~125,000 points). Realism is computed at the dataset level: all 50 frames are concatenated, masked to the track's point-cloud range, then subsampled to 10,000 points (seed 1234) before computing CD / MMD / EMD / FPD. Submitting denser frames does not improve scores; frame ordering does not matter.
  • The simplest valid naming is 0001.bin … 0050.bin.

predictions.json

JSON object whose keys are the frame IDs from detection_test_frame_ids.json (in the starting kit). For every frame ID you must include an entry, even if the value is an empty list.

{
  "<frame_id_1>": [
    {"box": [x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, heading], "score": 0.97, "class": "Car"},
    {"box": [...],                          "score": 0.81, "class": "Person"}
  ],
  "<frame_id_2>": [],
  ...
}
  • box: 7 floats, OpenPCDet convention. (x, y, z) is the box center in metres in the LiDAR frame, (dx, dy, dz) are full extents along the box-local axes, heading is rotation around +Z in radians.
  • score: confidence in [0, 1].
  • class: one of the valid class strings for this track. Valid values: Person, Car, Bicycle, Motorcycle, Bus, Truck, Van, Unknown. Class strings are matched case-insensitively. Predictions with unrecognized class strings are discarded before AP is computed.

declaration.pdf (or declaration.txt)

The starter kit ships declaration_template.pdf, a one-page form with the required honor statement preprinted and a signature line. Fill in team name and date, sign (digitally with any PDF tool, or print → sign → scan), save as declaration.pdf, and include it in every submission.

If you cannot easily produce a signed PDF, a plain declaration.txt is also accepted. Required statement (verbatim, case-insensitive):

I confirm that I did not train on any frame listed in forbidden_frames.txt, and that all submitted detections were produced by a model trained only on synthetic data I generated.

What gets returned

After scoring (typically < 5 minutes for valid submissions) you'll see your position on the leaderboard plus a Detailed Results view with all component metrics, including per-class AP.

提交格式

将以下所有内容打包成单个 submission.zip 文件，并在 提交 标签页上传。

submission.zip
├── synthetic/
│   ├── 0001.bin
│   ├── 0002.bin
│   ├── ...
│   └── 0050.bin           # 恰好 50 个文件
├── predictions.json
└── declaration.pdf        # 签名的诚信声明（PDF）。也接受 declaration.txt。

synthetic/<id>.bin

  • 恰好 50 个文件。
  • 每个文件为原始 float32 格式，形状 N × 3，行优先顺序，通道为 (x, y, z)，单位为米。
  • 接受 N × 3 或 N × 4（xyz + 强度）格式；如果存在强度列，在评分前会被丢弃。
  • 每个文件在磁盘上 ≤ 1.5 MB（约125,000个点）。真实感在数据集层面计算：所有50帧会被拼接，根据赛道的点云范围进行掩码，然后下采样至10,000个点（随机种子1234），再计算 CD / MMD / EMD / FPD。提交更密集的帧不会提高分数；帧的顺序无关紧要。
  • 最简单的有效命名为 0001.bin … 0050.bin。

predictions.json

JSON 对象的键为来自 detection_test_frame_ids.json（在起始工具包中）的帧 ID。对于每个帧 ID，必须包含一个条目，即使值为空列表。

{
  "<frame_id_1>": [
    {"box": [x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, heading], "score": 0.97, "class": "Car"},
    {"box": [...],                          "score": 0.81, "class": "Person"}
  ],
  "<frame_id_2>": [],
  ...
}
  • box：7 个浮点数，遵循 OpenPCDet 约定。(x, y, z) 是边界框在 LiDAR 坐标系中的中心位置（单位：米），(dx, dy, dz) 是沿边界框局部轴的完整尺寸，heading 是绕 +Z 轴的旋转角度（弧度）。
  • score：置信度，范围 [0, 1]。
  • class：该赛道的有效类别字符串之一。有效值：Person、Car、Bicycle、Motorcycle、Bus、Truck、Van、Unknown。类别字符串不区分大小写进行匹配。包含无法识别类别字符串的预测在计算 AP 之前会被丢弃。

declaration.pdf（或 declaration.txt）

起始工具包中提供 declaration_template.pdf，这是一份一页的表格，预印了所需的诚信声明和签名栏。填写队伍名称和日期，签名（使用任何 PDF 工具进行数字签名，或打印 → 签名 → 扫描），保存为 declaration.pdf，并包含在每次提交中。

如果您无法方便地生成签名 PDF，也接受纯文本的 declaration.txt。所需声明（原文照抄，不区分大小写）：

我确认未使用 forbidden_frames.txt 中列出的任何帧进行训练，且所有提交的检测结果均由仅使用我生成的合成数据训练的模型产生。

返回内容

评分完成后（有效提交通常在 5 分钟内），您将在排行榜上看到您的排名，以及包含所有 component 指标（包括每类 AP）的详细结果视图。

pages.title: Rules
pages.content:
Rules

Eligibility

  • Open to anyone — researchers, students, industry teams.
  • Each team must register one participant account; do not maintain multiple accounts.

Allowed

  • Any simulation framework or generative model (CARLA, Helios++, OpenScene, neural radiance fields, diffusion, GANs, custom physics). Open or closed source — what matters is the synthesized data.
  • Any 3D object detector architecture, trained on your synthetic data only.
  • Augmentations applied during detector training (rotation, scale, flip, ground-truth sampling, noise) — they operate on synthetic data, not on the forbidden real frames.
  • Using the train split of the public real dataset for hyperparameter selection or domain adaptation, provided no forbidden frame is touched. (The forbidden list contains only the 100 reserved frames, not the entire real train split.)

Forbidden

  • Training, validating, hyperparameter-tuning, or otherwise observing ground truth from any of the 100 frames listed in forbidden_frames.txt. This is enforced by signed declaration and is the foundational integrity rule of the challenge.
  • Submitting predictions produced by a model that has been trained on real labels for any roadside-LiDAR dataset. The detector must be sim-only.
  • Reverse-engineering or inferring the held-out realism reference frames via Codabench's leaderboard signal (e.g., probing submissions designed to leak the reference set's identity). Submissions found to be doing this will be disqualified.
  • Multiple accounts, sub-team accounts, or coordinating across registered teams.

Disqualification

Organizers reserve the right to inspect the synthetic frames and predictions of any submission for evidence of forbidden-frame leakage (e.g., synthetic frames that suspiciously resemble held-out real frames; predictions whose distribution implies access to held-out ground truth). Disqualified participants are removed from the leaderboard and from prize consideration.

Prizes

Per track: 1st place USD 500, 2nd place USD 300, 3rd place USD 200. Sponsor(s) will be announced before the Development phase opens.

Publication and credit

  • Every participating team submits a 4–8 page challenge report describing their approach, due by the final-phase deadline (November 15, 2026).
  • Teams that prefer not to publish may opt into the non-publication track for their submission.
  • Top-3 teams per track are invited to present at the IEEE BigData 2026 Big Data Cup workshop session in Phoenix, AZ (December 14–17, 2026), and to submit a full paper to the IEEE BigData 2026 proceedings through the challenge's associated paper track.
  • The challenge organizers may publish an aggregate analysis of all submissions (anonymized unless explicit permission is granted).

规则

参赛资格

  • 面向所有人开放——研究人员、学生、行业团队。
  • 每个团队必须注册一个参赛账户；请勿维护多个账户。

允许事项

  • 任何仿真框架或生成模型（CARLA、Helios++、OpenScene、神经辐射场、扩散模型、GAN、自定义物理）。无论开源或闭源——重要的是合成数据。
  • 任何三维目标检测器架构，仅使用您的合成数据进行训练。
  • 检测器训练期间应用的数据增强（旋转、缩放、翻转、真值采样、噪声）——它们作用于合成数据，而非禁止使用的真实帧。
  • 使用公开真实数据集的训练集划分进行超参数选择或域自适应，前提是不触碰任何禁止帧。（禁止列表仅包含100个保留帧，而非整个真实训练集划分。）

禁止事项

  • 对forbidden_frames.txt中列出的100帧中的任何一帧进行训练、验证、超参数调优或以其他方式观测真值。这通过签署声明强制执行，是本次挑战的基础完整性规则。
  • 提交使用任何路侧激光雷达数据集的真实标签训练的模型所产生的预测结果。检测器必须仅使用仿真数据。
  • 通过Codabench排行榜信号逆向工程或推断保留的真实感参考帧（例如，旨在泄露参考集身份的探测性提交）。发现此类行为的提交将被取消资格。
  • 多个账户、子团队账户，或跨注册团队协作。

取消资格

组织者保留检查任何提交的合成帧和预测结果的权利，以查找禁止帧泄露的证据（例如，与保留的真实帧惊人相似的合成帧；其分布暗示可访问保留真值的预测）。被取消资格的参与者将从排行榜和奖项评选中移除。

奖项

每个赛道：第一名500美元，第二名300美元，第三名200美元。赞助商将在开发阶段开始前公布。

发表与署名

  • 每个参赛团队提交一份4–8页的挑战报告，描述其方法，截止日期为最终阶段截止日期（2026年11月15日）。
  • 不愿发表的团队可以选择将其提交归入非发表赛道。
  • 每个赛道的前三名将获邀在亚利桑那州凤凰城举行的IEEE BigData 2026大数据杯研讨会（2026年12月14日至17日）上进行展示，并可通过挑战赛关联的论文通道向IEEE BigData 2026会议论文集提交完整论文。
  • 挑战赛组织者可以发表所有提交的汇总分析（除非获得明确许可，否则将匿名处理）。

# Registration > You must **first register** for Track 01 - EEG-to-Image before you can participate. **Registration takes three steps.** Open **Get Started → Registration Guide** in the menu on the left. Follow the approval instructions and, if applicable, the additional setup required for teams. --- # Before building a submission > To be evaluated successfully and appear on the leaderboard, every uploaded model must follow the **strict Codabench submission contract**. Before preparing and uploading your model, open **Get Started → Submission Guide** in the menu on the left. It defines the Python inference contract, output shape, trained weights, optional files, and validation workflow. The same guide and its executable examples are public in the **[2026 competition repository](https://github.com/neural-interfaces26/2026-competition)**. --- # After uploading: when will my score appear? > **Your submission may remain queued before evaluation starts.** All four tracks share the same evaluation queue, so your score may not appear immediately. Once started, Track 01 normally needs 2–3 additional minutes to load and prepare the evaluation data, plus the model's inference time. You can leave the page and return later; refreshing the Codabench webpage will not accelerate the evaluation process. --- # Track 01 · EEG-to-Image > **Sealed-phase specification.** The description, task contract, and ranking metric below define the final sealed phase. Warm-up uses a closely matched Top-5 retrieval proxy on public THINGS-EEG2 data. Its candidate set and aggregation are detailed below. _Identify a viewed natural image from a single EEG response._ Given one multichannel EEG epoch recorded during natural-image viewing, predict a **1536-dimensional DINOv2-giant image embedding**. Codabench compares that prediction with the frozen embeddings of the candidate image gallery. The sealed split contains participants and images absent from training, testing cross-participant and cross-stimulus transfer rather than memorization of a fixed catalogue.

## Sealed-phase task contract | | | | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Input** | One multichannel EEG epoch | | **Prediction** | One 1536-dimensional DINOv2-giant embedding | | **Objective** | Retrieve the viewed image from the complete candidate gallery | | **Generalization shift** | New participants and images | | **Sealed split** | Evaluation participants and images are absent from training | ## Sealed-phase ranking metric > **Top-5 retrieval accuracy. Higher is better.** For each EEG epoch, Codabench L2-normalizes the predicted embedding and the frozen DINOv2-giant embeddings in its held-out candidate gallery, then ranks their cosine similarities. A query is correct when the viewed image is among the five highest-ranked candidates. Predictions for repeated presentations of the same image are aggregated within each subject before retrieval, then the subject-level results are averaged so that every subject contributes equally. Top-1 accuracy is reported separately but does not determine the ranking. ## Development, warm-up, and sealed data **Development and training.** You may train your model on any of the organizer-recommended public datasets in the **[main website’s dataset directory](https://neural-interfaces26.github.io/tracks.html#datasets)** or other data permitted by the Terms. The public **[Track 01 competition directory](https://github.com/neural-interfaces26/2026-competition/tree/main/tracks/image_decoding)** contains the executable contract and metric, dataset adapters, editable worked solvers, Benchopt configs, and NeuralBench checkpoint wrapper. **Warm-up evaluation.** Warm-up submissions on Codabench are currently being evaluated on a subset of the public **THINGS-EEG2** dataset. This evaluation subset matches the test set in the [Track 01 NeuralBench start kit](https://facebookresearch.github.io/neuroai/neuralbench/auto_examples/biosignal_challenge_2026/plot_track1_eeg_to_image.html): timelines marked as test form the Codabench evaluation partition, while 20% of the training timelines are assigned to validation using random state 33. Codabench ranks each epoch against the unique target-image embeddings in that test partition and reports pooled Top-5 accuracy across all evaluation epochs. Unlike the sealed metric and NeuralBench's headline `test/full_retrieval/top5_acc_subject-agg`, this temporary proxy does not aggregate repeated presentations within subjects. Top-1 accuracy is reported separately. THINGS-EEG2 also provides the **[reported public baseline scores](https://neural-interfaces26.github.io/participant-guide.html#baseline-track-1)**. Because the test data and labels are public, leakage is possible and warm-up scores are indicative only. Only the sealed phase determines the final ranking. **Sealed evaluation.** Codabench switches to the private 2026 Alljoined cohort described in the **[main website’s dataset directory](https://neural-interfaces26.github.io/tracks.html#dataset-track-1)**. This cohort is uploaded only for the sealed phase, and its participants, images, and labels remain hidden. ## Track resources and next steps **[Explore the full Track 01 description on the main website →](https://neural-interfaces26.github.io/tracks.html#track-1)** · **[Choose a repository workflow →](https://github.com/neural-interfaces26/2026-competition/blob/main/tracks/README.md)** · **[Use the NeuralBench start kit and public baselines →](https://facebookresearch.github.io/neuroai/neuralbench/auto_examples/biosignal_challenge_2026/plot_track1_eeg_to_image.html)** · **[Review prizes and conditions →](https://neural-interfaces26.github.io/prizes.html#award-track-1)** For packaging and uploads, use **Get Started → Submission Guide**. For current dates and submission limits, use **Phases**. For eligibility, data use, and the reproducibility audit, use **Terms**. --- ## Track partners ### Sponsor and scientific institutions        **Alljoined** sponsors Track 01 and provides its 2026 hidden evaluation cohort. **Meta FAIR Brain & AI** leads the track’s scientific development. ### Organizing institutions

# Register in three steps **Every participant must complete these steps, whether entering individually or as part of a team. Registration remains open through October 24, 2026, during the warm-up phase.** 1. Create a **[Codabench account](https://www.codabench.org/accounts/signup)** and sign in. 2. Open **My Submissions** for every track you wish to enter: **[Track 01](https://www.codabench.org/competitions/17974/#/participate-tab)**, **[Track 02](https://www.codabench.org/competitions/17982/#/participate-tab)**, **[Track 03](https://www.codabench.org/competitions/17983/#/participate-tab)**, or **[Track 04](https://www.codabench.org/competitions/17984/#/participate-tab)**. On each page, accept the terms and conditions, then click **Register**. Your request will appear as **pending**. 3. Submit the **[registration form](https://forms.gle/p3t2V25nuQtVXyj9A)**. If you are entering multiple tracks, submit it once and select every track for which you registered. In the form, enter the exact email address associated with your Codabench account. You may open the form using another email account, but approval uses the address entered in the form. Return to **My Submissions** for each track to confirm your registration. Refresh the page if needed. # Entering as a team? **Individual participants can skip this section.** 1. Every team member completes the three registration steps above individually. pages.title: Submission Guide
pages.content:
# How to submit your model

## Submission rules

Upload a **fully trained model as a ZIP** through the **My Submissions** tab.
Codabench will mount the extracted files as read-only, run the model in inference
mode, compute the track metric, and publish the score. It does not train
your model.

Your typical `my_submission.zip` contains:

```text
my_submission.zip
├── submission.py   # required: all Python inference code
├── weights.pt      # trained parameters, with any name or format
└── ...             # optional non-Python artifact like config.json
```

- Put every file at the **root of the ZIP**.
- `submission.py` must contain `class Solver(CompetSolver)`, the model
  architecture, model-specific preprocessing, and all Python inference code.
  Additional Python modules are not supported. See below for more details.
- Include every weight and optional non-Python artifact the model needs. Read
  them from `meta["submission_dir"]` in `submission.py`.

Nothing is installed during evaluation, so `submission.py` may only import
what the worker image already carries — `torch` and the rest of the stack
pinned in
[`requirements.txt`](https://github.com/neural-interfaces26/2026-competition/blob/main/requirements.txt).
During `load_model` and `predict`, do not train, do not download competition
data, and do not write into the submission directory.

**Submission storage limit.** Codabench gives each profile 15 GB of submission
storage shared across all tracks and uploads; it is not a separate 15 GB limit
for each ZIP. This makes 15 GB the theoretical maximum for one submission,
but the practical limit is the space remaining in your profile. If needed,
delete unused archived submissions under **Profile → Resources**. A submission
displayed on a leaderboard cannot be deleted.

The public **[2026 competition repository](https://github.com/neural-interfaces26/2026-competition)**
is the executable companion to this guide. Start with its
**[shared track workflows](https://github.com/neural-interfaces26/2026-competition/blob/main/tracks/README.md)**,
then open your track directory for the metric and contract, supported public
datasets, editable worked solvers, Benchopt configs, and NeuralBench checkpoint
wrapper.

---

## Submit in five steps

1. **Train and validate locally** with a NeuralBench start kit, the Benchopt
   competition kit, both, or your own pipeline. Save the trained weights. The
   repository's [shared track workflows](https://github.com/neural-interfaces26/2026-competition/blob/main/tracks/README.md)
   explain each route. If your Benchopt solver implements the optional `fit`
   and `save_model` methods described below, its training run writes the
   solver and weights into a ready-to-upload submission folder for you.
2. **Create `submission.py`** following the contract below.
3. **Create the ZIP.** For the example above, run:

   ```bash
   zip -j my_submission.zip submission.py weights.pt
   ```

   Add `config.json` or any other non-Python artifact your model needs.

4. **Check it locally first.** A failed upload still costs you one of the
   day's submissions, and most failures are caught in seconds:

   ```bash
   COMPET_SUBMISSION_DIR="$PWD/my_submission" \
       benchopt run tracks/<track> -d Simulated \
       -s "$PWD/my_submission/submission.py"
   ```

   See [Test your submission locally](#test-your-submission-locally) for
   what this does and does not cover.

5. **Upload.** In **My Submissions**, select the active phase, upload the
   ZIP, and wait for **Finished**. If it fails, start with the first error
   in the ingestion log.

---

## The `submission.py` contract

In `submission.py`, you write ordinary Python or PyTorch code. Benchopt
provides the evaluation wrapper, but you do not need to understand its
internals. Codabench expects two components:

1. A named `class Solver(CompetSolver)` implementing `load_model(meta)`.
2. A model returned by `load_model` and exposing `predict(X)`.

### Contract 1: `class Solver(CompetSolver)` loads the trained model

In `class Solver(CompetSolver)`, **`load_model(self, meta) -> model` is
required**. It reconstructs the trained architecture, loads the shipped
weights, moves the model to the evaluation device, and returns it in
evaluation mode:

```python
import torch

from benchmark_utils.base_solver import CompetSolver

class Solver(CompetSolver):
    name = "MyModel"

    def load_model(self, meta):
        # MyModel must be defined in this submission.py file or imported
        # from a dependency.
        model = MyModel(
            n_chans=meta["n_chans"],
            n_times=meta["n_times"],
        )
        weights = meta["submission_dir"] / "weights.pt"
        state_dict = torch.load(
            weights,
            map_location=meta["device"],
            weights_only=True,
        )
        model.load_state_dict(state_dict)
        return model.to(meta["device"]).eval()

    # Optional local-training hooks. Codabench never calls them.
    # See "Practice 2: Train and package with Benchopt" below.
    def fit(self, model, train_loader):
        ...

    def save_model(self, model, path):
        ...
```

Each track's [`solvers/`](https://github.com/neural-interfaces26/2026-competition/tree/main/tracks)
directory holds working implementations of this contract on real data —
the closest reference for your own `submission.py`.

Remark: `meta` is a plain Python dictionary created and passed to `load_model`
automatically. You do not create or upload it. It provides:

- `submission_dir`: read-only path to the files extracted from your ZIP
- `device`: CPU or GPU used for the model and input batches
- `n_chans`, `n_times`, `sfreq`, `ch_names`, `chs_info`: input description
- `n_outputs`, `n_classes`, or `n_joints`: track-specific output size

A fixed-size architecture normally uses `meta["n_chans"]` and
`meta["n_times"]`. A shape-agnostic model may infer these dimensions from `X`.

### Contract 2: The built model generates predictions

After `Solver.load_model(meta)` returns your model, Codabench calls that
required model's `predict(X)` method for every evaluation batch.

`X` is a PyTorch tensor already on `meta["device"]`, with shape `(B, C, T)`:

- `B`: batch size
- `C`: signal channels
- `T`: time samples

`predict(X)` must return the output required by the track:

| Track             | `predict(X)` must return                   | Output-size key           | Final sealed metric      |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| 01 - EEG-to-Image | image embeddings `(B, D)`                  | `meta["n_outputs"]` = `D` | top-5 retrieval accuracy |
| 02 - BCI Decoding | one class index per window `(B,)`          | `meta["n_classes"]`       | balanced accuracy        |
| 03 - Sleep Onset  | seconds to sleep onset `(B,)` as floats    | `meta["n_outputs"]` = `1` | weighted binned MAE      |
| 04 - EMG-to-Pose  | joint angles `(B, n_joints, T)` in radians | `meta["n_joints"]`        | mean angular MAE, reported in degrees |

**Track 04 unit contract:** `predict(X)` must return joint angles in radians.
Do not convert predictions to degrees. Codabench computes the MAE from the
radian predictions and targets, then converts only the final aggregate score
to degrees for the leaderboard.

Warm-up proxy metrics may differ. The **Track description** tab gives the
active warm-up metric and the final sealed specification for each track.

A PyTorch model can implement `predict` directly:

```python
class MyModel(torch.nn.Module):
    @torch.inference_mode()
    def predict(self, X):
        self.eval()
        return self(X)
```

---

## Behind the scenes: How Codabench and Benchopt evaluate your submission

[Benchopt](https://benchopt.github.io) runs each public track benchmark and
computes its metrics. Codabench manages uploads, workers, and leaderboards.

Only the sealed evaluation data and labels are hidden. The submission
contract remains stable, while the evaluation data and, for proxy warm-ups,
the task or metric may differ by phase:

|                                 | Warm-up phase                    | Sealed final phase                       |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Evaluation data                 | development or public proxy data | held-out cohort, never released          |
| Benchmark framework and worker image | public competition stack      | same competition stack                   |
| Task and ranking metric         | public proxy; see Track description | final specification; see Track description |
| `meta` keys and tensor contract | documented contract              | same contract, runtime values may differ |
| Submission ZIP format           | same contract                     | same contract                            |

Tracks 01–03 currently have phase-specific proxy details. Track 04 uses the
same prediction task and metric in both phases, on different evaluation data.

For portability, **use only `meta` and the provided batches**. Do not rely on
undocumented dataset names, paths, subject identifiers, or fixed dimensions.

---

## Get some practice

The repository's [shared track guide](https://github.com/neural-interfaces26/2026-competition/blob/main/tracks/README.md)
connects the NeuralBench and Benchopt routes. Each track README then documents
its contract, data choices, reference results, and worked models:
[Track 01](https://github.com/neural-interfaces26/2026-competition/tree/main/tracks/image_decoding),
[Track 02](https://github.com/neural-interfaces26/2026-competition/tree/main/tracks/bci_decoding),
[Track 03](https://github.com/neural-interfaces26/2026-competition/tree/main/tracks/sleep_onset),
and [Track 04](https://github.com/neural-interfaces26/2026-competition/tree/main/tracks/emg_pose).

These files show the submission contract, but they are at different stages:
each track has an uploadable dependency-light floor, while neural models need
a trained checkpoint before they represent a baseline.
The `examples/` directory is not stored in Git. It is created only inside a
generated starting-kit archive by `tools/make_starting_kit.py`. The generator
includes trained weights only when they already exist under the track's
`outputs/` directory; otherwise it warns that the example is untrained.

Every track ships the same four-rung progression, from an upload-ready floor to
a trained neural network. Copy the rung closest to what you want and adapt it:

| Rung | What it shows | 01 · Image | 02 · BCI | 03 · Sleep | 04 · EMG |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Constant floor | the contract with no weights and no training | `mean_embedding.py` | `constant.py` | `median_baseline.py` | `mean_pose.py` |
| scikit-learn linear | a linear model, weights saved as a joblib dump | `mean_ridge.py` | `mean_logreg.py` | `mean_ridge.py` | `ridge_pose.py` |
| Torch linear | the same idea in PyTorch, with its own `fit` / `save_model` | `torch_linear.py` | `torch_linear.py` | `torch_linear.py` | `torch_linear.py` |
| EEGNet | a NeuralBench-compatible architecture and inference wrapper, trained end-to-end | `eegnet_clip.py` | `eegnet.py` | `eegnet_reg.py` | `eegnet_pose.py` |
| Frozen foundation probe | pretrained REVE with a fitted joblib head | `reve_probe.py` | `reve_probe.py` | `reve_probe.py` | not applicable |

**Which path should you train with?** Choose by workflow, not architecture.
NeuralBench offers neuro-specific tasks, preprocessing, adaptation, catalogue
models, and custom-model evaluation. The Benchopt competition kit runs
included or custom models directly against the executable competition and can
export the submission. You may combine them or use your own pipeline. Every
route ends with the same self-contained `submission.py` plus weights.

### Practice 1: Check the platform with a constant baseline

Start with the dependency-light floor for your track:

- Track 01: `mean_embedding.py`
- Track 02: `constant.py`
- Track 03: `median_baseline.py`
- Track 04: `mean_pose.py`

Copy the selected file to `submission.py`, place it at the root of a ZIP,
and upload it through **My Submissions**. A successful run confirms ZIP
ingestion, inference, scoring, and leaderboard publication before you package
your own model. Without weights, these examples deliberately return a trivial
constant prediction. Train them through Practice 2 to save and reload a fitted
floor instead.

### Practice 2: Train and package with Benchopt

Benchopt already evaluates your submission; it can package it too.
Rather than assembling the ZIP by hand as in step 3 above, implement
two optional methods and a local run writes it for you — `torch_linear.py`
and `mean_ridge.py` are the worked examples. During that run:

- `fit(model, train_loader)` trains the model
- `save_model(model, path)` saves its weights
- `CompetSolver` writes the solver and weights into a submission folder

Codabench never calls `fit` or `save_model` — the server is
inference-only — so they cost you nothing at evaluation time. If you
train and package another way, omit both.

Run the commands below from the repository root after completing the
[optional local Benchopt setup](https://github.com/neural-interfaces26/2026-competition#optional-local-benchopt-setup).

For a fast end-to-end check with no public-data download, the repository can
train an EEGNet-style model on tiny synthetic data using the real warm-up
tensor dimensions, reload the exported checkpoint, and create an uploadable
ZIP:

```bash
python tools/debug_submission.py --track <track>
```

Use `--all` to build all four, or add `--model reve` to build the three EEG
tracks with a frozen REVE encoder. These models validate the workflow only;
their scores have no scientific meaning.

First, a one-command check that your setup works — the dummy baseline on the
`Simulated` data, no download:

```bash
benchopt install tracks/<track> --config tracks/<track>/starter.yml -y
benchopt run tracks/<track> --config tracks/<track>/starter.yml
```

Then train for real. Each track ships a **training config** —
`tracks/<track>/training.yml` — that pins the public warm-up dataset and turns
training on. Copy a baseline into `solvers/`, rename its `Solver` to `MyModel`,
then prepare the data and train it into a ready-to-upload submission through that
config:

```bash
benchopt install tracks/<track> --config tracks/<track>/training.yml -y
benchopt prepare tracks/<track> --config tracks/<track>/training.yml
benchopt run     tracks/<track> --config tracks/<track>/training.yml -s MyModel
```

`-s MyModel` overrides the config's baseline solver; drop it to train the
baseline itself. The config hides the dataset and `training=True` flags — if you
ever need the names by hand:

| Track | `<track>`        | `<objective>`    |
| ----- | ---------------- | ---------------- |
| 01    | `image_decoding` | `Image-decoding` |
| 02    | `bci_decoding`   | `BCI-decoding`   |
| 03    | `sleep_onset`    | `Sleep-onset`    |
| 04    | `emg_pose`       | `EMG-pose`       |

**Train on different data.** The config uses each track's default public study.
To train on another study — or your own data — override the dataset with `-d`
(it replaces the config's dataset); these are the same datasets named in the
[participant guide](https://neural-interfaces26.github.io/participant-guide.html):

| Track | `-d` data source | What it is |
| ----- | ---------------- | ---------- |
| 01 | `"Image[study=gifford2022large]"` | THINGS-EEG2 (Gifford2022Large) — public proxy, **default** |
| 01 | `"Image[study=grootswagers2022human]"`, `"…[study=xu2024alljoined]"`, `"…[study=xu2025alljoined]"` | alternative public studies |
| 02 | `"BCI[study=dreyer2023]"` | Dreyer2023Large — the **warm-up evaluation** study, **default** |
| 02 | `"BCI[study=stieger2021]"` | Stieger2021Continuous — additional 4-class public proxy |
| 02 | `"BCI[study=tangermann2012]"` | BNCI2014_001 — small, for real-data smoke tests |
| 03 | `"Sleep-EDF"` | Sleep-EDF (Kemp2000Analysis) |
| 04 | `"Salter2024Emg2pose"` | public EMG2Pose |
| any | `Simulated` | tiny synthetic set — contract check only, no download |
| any | `path/to/my_dataset.py` | your own benchopt Dataset, loaded straight from the file |

```bash
benchopt prepare tracks/<track> -d "<data source>"
benchopt run     tracks/<track> -d "<data source>" -s MyModel -o "<objective>[training=True]"
```

Plain `-d Simulated` uses deliberately small default dimensions and is the
fastest code-contract check, but a fixed-size model trained that way will not
fit the real task. Use `tools/debug_submission.py` for an uploadable synthetic
workflow check, or train on a real study for a meaningful model.

For a solver implementing `save_model`, the training run writes a
ready-to-upload submission folder (`submission.py` plus its weights). Zip its
contents, not the enclosing folder, to upload:

```text
tracks/<track>/outputs/<model-name>/
```

Benchopt does more than package: parameter sweeps, cached reruns, plots and
SLURM execution are summarised in
[Develop further with Benchopt](#develop-further-with-benchopt) at the end
of this page.

### Optional practice 3: Reproduce the NeuralBench start kit

Follow the matching [NeuralBench competition start kit](https://facebookresearch.github.io/neuroai/neuralbench/auto_examples/biosignal_challenge_2026/index.html)
and retain or export its best checkpoint. This repository provides unchanged
Codabench inference wrappers for the start-kit models: EEGNet for Tracks 01–03
and VEMG2Pose for Track 04.

Copy the matching file from `tracks/<track>/submission_templates/` to
`submission.py`, add the checkpoint as `weights.pt`, and ZIP those two files.
Benchopt is not required for this manual packaging route. The repository's
[NeuralBench-to-Codabench bridge](https://github.com/neural-interfaces26/2026-competition/blob/main/tracks/README.md#package-a-neuralbench-checkpoint)
lists the exact wrapper for each track, accepted checkpoint formats, commands,
and an optional local replay.

## Test your submission locally

Local testing is optional, but catches missing files, imports, and incorrect
output shapes.

Clone or download the
[competition repository](https://github.com/neural-interfaces26/2026-competition).
If a generated track starting kit is also provided, it uses the same
`tracks/<track>/` layout and additionally contains derived submission ZIPs
under `examples/`. From the repository or an extracted kit root:

```bash
benchopt install tracks/<track>  # add --gpu if your setup requires CUDA
COMPET_SUBMISSION_DIR="$PWD/my_submission" \
    benchopt run tracks/<track> -d Simulated \
    -s "$PWD/my_submission/submission.py"
```

`COMPET_SUBMISSION_DIR` makes
`meta["submission_dir"]` point at the folder containing your weights and
optional artifacts. `Simulated` requires no download.
It is a quick contract check, not an official score. A fixed-size checkpoint
trained for the real task may be incompatible with the smaller simulated
dimensions; validate such a model on matching public track data instead. To
exercise the complete train, export, reload, and ZIP path without downloading
that data, use `python tools/debug_submission.py --track <track>`. Dropping a
solver next to the track's own baselines remains useful for comparisons:
selectors are case-insensitive globs, so `-s MyModel -s "eegnet*"` runs yours
against every EEGNet baseline the track ships.

---

## Common submission errors

- `submission.py` or the weights are inside an extra directory in the ZIP
- `class Solver` is missing, renamed, or cannot be imported
- the filename loaded in `load_model` does not match the uploaded weight file
- the model imports a package that is not available in the worker image
- the model or input is placed on the wrong device
- `predict(X)` returns the wrong shape, type, or unit for the track
- the submission tries to train, download data, or write into its read-only
  directory during server evaluation

If ingestion fails, start with the **first error in the log**. Later messages
such as a missing `results.parquet` usually mean that inference already
failed and no results file could be created.

---

## Optional: use a large pretrained EEG model

`braindecode` ships pretrained models including REVE, BENDR, BIOT, CBraMod,
and SignalJEPA. When a checkpoint is too large for the submission ZIP,
`Model.from_pretrained(...)` can retrieve its published weights from the
Hugging Face Hub. Models listed in the repository's
[`staged_hf_models.txt`](https://github.com/neural-interfaces26/2026-competition/blob/main/tools/staged_hf_models.txt)
are cached on competition workers. Other weights may download during each
submission and count against the one-hour evaluation limit, so prefer shipping
them when feasible.

---

## Develop further with Benchopt

Starting kits are standard [Benchopt](https://benchopt.github.io)
benchmarks. Benchopt supports parameter sweeps, cached reruns, interactive
reports with `benchopt plot`, reproducible YAML configurations, and local or
SLURM execution. These features are optional. See the
[Benchopt competition workflow](https://github.com/neural-interfaces26/2026-competition/blob/main/tracks/README.md#develop-and-package-with-benchopt)
for the full workflow. For AI tools, `benchopt sync-skills --global` installs
Benchopt solver conventions.

# 如何提交你的模型

## 提交规则

通过**我的提交**标签页上传一个**完全训练的模型ZIP文件**。
Codabench会将解压后的文件以只读方式挂载，在推理模式下运行模型，计算赛道指标，并发布分数。它不会训练你的模型。

你典型的`my_submission.zip`包含：

```text
my_submission.zip
├── submission.py   # 必需：所有Python推理代码
├── weights.pt      # 训练参数，任何名称或格式均可
└── ...             # 可选的非Python产物，如config.json
```

- 将所有文件放在**ZIP根目录**。
- `submission.py`必须包含`class Solver(CompetSolver)`、模型架构、模型特定的预处理以及所有Python推理代码。不支持额外的Python模块。详见下文。
- 包含模型所需的每个权重和可选的非Python产物。在`submission.py`中从`meta["submission_dir"]`读取它们。

评估期间不会安装任何东西，因此`submission.py`只能导入工作镜像已携带的内容——`torch`以及固定在[`requirements.txt`](https://github.com/neural-interfaces26/2026-competition/blob/main/requirements.txt)中的其他软件栈。在`load_model`和`predict`期间，不要训练，不要下载竞赛数据，也不要写入提交目录。

**提交存储限制。** Codabench为每个配置文件提供15 GB的提交存储空间，在所有赛道和上传之间共享；不是每个ZIP单独的15 GB限制。这使得15 GB成为一次提交的理论最大值，但实际限制是你配置文件中剩余的空间。如有需要，在**配置文件 → 资源**下删除未使用的已归档提交。显示在排行榜上的提交无法删除。

---

## 五步提交

1. **在本地训练和验证**，使用可选的NeuralBench启动套件、直接通过Benchopt或使用你自己的流程。保存训练好的权重。如果你的Benchopt求解器实现了下文描述的可选`fit`和`save_model`方法，其训练运行会将求解器和权重写入一个准备上传的提交文件夹中。
2. **创建`submission.py`**，遵循下文合约。
3. **创建ZIP。**对于上述示例，运行：

   ```bash
   zip -j my_submission.zip submission.py weights.pt
   ```

   添加`config.json`或模型需要的任何其他非Python产物。

4. **先在本地检查。**上传失败仍会消耗你当日提交次数中的一次，而且大多数失败会在几秒钟内被发现：

   ```bash
   cp my_submission/submission.py tracks/<track>/solvers/my_submission.py
   COMPET_SUBMISSION_DIR="$PWD/my_submission" \
       benchopt run tracks/<track> -d Simulated -s MyModel
   ```

   有关这涵盖和不涵盖的内容，请参阅[在本地测试你的提交](#test-your-submission-locally)。

5. **上传。**在**我的提交**中，选择活跃阶段，上传ZIP，并等待**完成**。如果失败，从摄取日志中的第一个错误开始排查。

---

## `submission.py`合约

在`submission.py`中，你编写普通的Python或PyTorch代码。Benchopt提供评估包装器，但你不需要了解其内部机制。Codabench期望两个组件：

1. 一个命名了的`class Solver(CompetSolver)`，实现`load_model(meta)`。
2. 一个由`load_model`返回并暴露`predict(X)`的模型。

### 合约1：`class Solver(CompetSolver)`加载训练好的模型

在`class Solver(CompetSolver)`中，**`load_model(self, meta) -> model`是必需的**。它重建训练好的架构，加载随附的权重，将模型移动到评估设备，并以评估模式返回：

```python

from benchmark_utils.base_solver import CompetSolver
```

# Timeline

## Warm-up phase

**Sep 21 to Oct 25, 2026**

Codabench evaluates submissions on public, track-specific test data during warm-up. Because these data and labels are public, overlap or leakage is possible. Use the indicative leaderboard to validate the submission workflow and iterate on your model. Warm-up scores do not determine the final ranking.

**Submission limit:** Up to five submissions per participant per day.

## Sealed final phase

**Oct 28 to Nov 21, 2026, Anywhere on Earth**

Codabench switches to the private 2026 evaluation cohorts, which are uploaded only for this phase. Their examples and labels remain hidden. Only sealed-phase scores determine the final ranking, using the best of each team’s last five sealed submissions.

**Submission limit:** One submission per participant per day.

## Reproducibility audit

**After Nov 21, 2026**

The top three teams in each track undergo a reproducibility audit. Organizers rerun the submitted training pipeline and evaluate the resulting model weights on the sealed test set.

## Winners’ ceremony

**Dec 11 and 12, 2026**

The winners will be announced during the Brain and Body Workshop at NeurIPS 2026 in Sydney.

# 🩺 
# **OncoSegment: Breast Tumor Mapping Challenge**

# 💡 
## **Why this Problem is Interesting**

Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of death among women worldwide. Early and accurate detection through ultrasound is critical, but interpreting these images is notoriously difficult.Ultrasound images suffer from "speckle noise" and low contrast. Much like the "blobs" in plasma physics simulations, tumors in ultrasound are intermittent, have irregular boundaries, and can be easily confused with healthy tissue. This challenge asks you to develop an AI that can precisely outline tumor boundaries, a task that directly assists radiologists in biopsy planning and treatment.

# 📊 
## **The Data**

The dataset is derived from the Breast Ultrasound Images (BUSI) collection, featuring women aged 25–75. It consists of high-quality PNG scans with a standard resolution (approx. 500x500 px).

Dataset Breakdown:

Benign: Tumors that are typically oval or round with smooth edges.

Malignant: Cancerous tumors, often characterized by "spiky" (spiculated) or irregular borders that invade surrounding tissue.

Normal: Scans with no tumors (used to test your model's ability to avoid False Positives).

What you receive in the Starting Kit:
train_images: A list of PIL images (Grayscale) showing the breast 
tissue.
train_masks: Binary masks where 1 represents the tumor and 0 represents the background.
train_labels: Metadata identifying the tumor as benign or malignant.
test_images: Images where you must predict the mask.

 # 📏 
## **Metrics: Measuring Precision**

In medical imaging, a "box" is not enough. We need to know exactly which pixels are cancerous. We use two complementary overlap metrics:
1. Primary Metric: Dice Coefficient (F1-Score)The Dice coefficient is the gold standard for medical segmentation. It is twice the area of overlap divided by the total number of pixels in both the prediction and the ground truth.
$$Dice = \frac{2 \times |P \cap G|}{|P| + |G|}$$
Why? It is highly sensitive to the internal "fullness" of the mask and rewards models that get the shape exactly right.
2. Secondary Metric: Jaccard Index (IoU)
The Jaccard index is the area of intersection divided by the area of union.
$$Jaccard = \frac{|P \cap G|}{|P \cup G|}$$
Why? 
It is more "punishing" than Dice for small errors.
It helps break ties on the leaderboard by highlighting models with the fewest stray False Positive pixels.

# 🩺 
# **OncoSegment: 乳腺肿瘤分割挑战赛**

# 💡 
## **该问题的研究价值**

乳腺癌仍是全球女性死亡的主要原因之一。通过超声进行早期和准确检测至关重要，但解读这些图像却 notoriously 困难。超声图像存在"散斑噪声"且对比度低。正如等离子体物理模拟中的"团块"一样，超声中的肿瘤呈间歇性分布，边界不规则，且容易与正常健康组织混淆。本挑战要求你开发能够精确勾勒肿瘤边界的人工智能，该任务可直接辅助放射科医生进行活检规划与治疗。

# 📊 
## **数据**

数据集源自乳腺超声图像（BUSI）数据集，研究对象为25-75岁女性。包含高质量的PNG扫描图像，标准分辨率约为500×500像素。

数据集构成：

良性：通常为椭圆形或圆形、边缘光滑的肿瘤。

恶性：癌性肿瘤，通常以"毛刺状"（spiculated）或侵入周围组织的不规则边界为特征。

正常：无肿瘤的扫描图像（用于测试模型避免假阳性的能力）。

入门套件包含：
train_images：一系列显示乳腺组织的PIL图像（灰度）。
train_masks：二值掩膜，其中1代表肿瘤，0代表背景。
train_labels：元数据，用于识别肿瘤为良性或恶性。
test_images：需要预测掩膜的图像。

 # 📏 
## **评估指标：精确度测量**

在医学影像中，简单的"框选"是不够的。我们需要确切知道哪些像素是癌性的。我们采用两种互补的重叠指标：
1. 主要指标：Dice系数（F1分数）
Dice系数是医学分割领域的黄金标准。计算方法为预测与真实值重叠区域面积的两倍，除以预测与真实值的总像素数。
$$Dice = \frac{2 \times |P \cap G|}{|P| + |G|}$$
原因：该指标对掩膜内部的"充实度"高度敏感，能够奖励形状完全精确的模型。
2. 次要指标：Jaccard指数（IoU）
Jaccard指数是交集面积除以并集面积。
$$Jaccard = \frac{|P \cap G|}{|P \cup G|}$$
原因：
相比Dice，它对微小错误更为"严苛"。
有助于在排行榜上打破平局，突出显示具有最少杂散假阳性像素的模型。
